items.statement: Q4 FY25 GMV grew 27% year-on-year to INR4,102 crores.
items.quote: Starting with One Nykaa highlights, happy to say that the GMV for the fourth quarter continued to grow at a fast pace of 27% year-on-year growth and the GMV for the quarter was INR4,102 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 net revenue grew 24% year-on-year to INR2,062 crores.
items.quote: Net revenue similarly showed a 24% year-on-year growth coming out at INR2,062 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 gross margin was 44.1%, up 151 basis points year-on-year.
items.quote: Gross margins were healthy at 44.1% for the One Nykaa. And this reflects an improvement of 151 basis points on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA was INR133 crores, 6.5% of revenue, up 43% year-on-year.
items.quote: EBITDA has come out at INR133 crores for the quarter. That's a 6.5% EBITDA on a percentage to revenue basis, and that's about a 43% year-on-year growth, improving profit margins compared to the revenue growth.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 PAT was INR19 crores, 0.9% of net revenue, up 110% year-on-year.
items.quote: And finally, on the PAT at INR19 crores PAT with 0.9% of net revenue and a year-on-year growth of 110%.

items.statement: FY25 GMV grew 25% to INR15,604 crores.
items.quote: Next, the results for the full year are similar with a 25% growth in GMV with the GMV of One Nykaa at INR15,604 crores.

items.statement: FY25 net revenue grew 24% to INR7,950 crores.
items.quote: Net revenue came out at INR7,950 crores, almost $1 billion revenues, and that showed a 24% year-on-year growth on a full year basis.

items.statement: FY25 gross margin was 43.7%, up 84 basis points annually.
items.quote: Gross margin came out at 43.7%, an 84 basis point improvement on an annual basis.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA was INR474 crores, 6% of net revenue, up 37% year-on-year.
items.quote: And EBITDA for the full year at INR474 crores, that's a 6 percentage of net revenue and 37% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: FY25 PAT was INR72 crores, 0.9% of net revenue, up 81% year-on-year.
items.quote: On the PAT, the PAT is at INR72 crores, again, 0.9% of net revenue and a 81% year-on-year growth on a full year basis.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 Beauty GMV grew 31% to INR3,058 crores.
items.quote: Beauty has had a strong year, growing at 31% in the fourth quarter to result in a GMV of INR3,058 crores.

items.statement: FY25 Beauty GMV grew 30% to INR11,775 crores.
items.quote: And similarly, the full year growth has come out at 30%, and that's about INR11,775 crores GMV.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 Fashion GMV grew 18% year-on-year.
items.quote: The fourth quarter GMV improvement in fashion is 18% year-on-year growth, a revival from the previous quarter.

items.statement: FY25 Fashion GMV grew 12% to INR3,804 crores.
items.quote: And similarly, for the full year, the fashion growth has come out at 12% on a year-on-year basis -- on a GMV basis at INR3,804 crores of GMV, total GMV.

items.statement: FY25 own beauty brands GMV was INR1,700 crores, up 55% year-on-year.
items.quote: In FY '25, this portfolio has now achieved about INR1,700 crores of GMV, showing a 55% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 own beauty brands GMV was INR526 crores, up 72% year-on-year.
items.quote: In quarter 4 itself, there was an acceleration further, and there's been a 72% year-on-year growth, taking the GMV for Q4 to INR526 crores.

items.statement: Beauty vertical margin outlook depends on mix; own brands and eB2B growing faster could pressure consolidated margins.
items.quote: So the outlook for the margin profile for the entire vertical is, in a way, also an outcome of the way that the mix evolves. Some of -- in a way, the mix is really at play here. Its own brands and eB2B, which currently have a lower margin profile than the multi-brand retail business. If they continue to grow faster than the retail business, tha t could put some downward pressure on margins at the

items.statement: Nykaa Now rapid delivery live in multiple metros, good traction, plans to expand to more metros.
items.quote: Today, that is live in multiple cities, majorly the metros. And we have seen relatively good traction. And a good percentage of our orders are now being fulfilled in those metros which are being serviced through Nykaa Now through this rapid delivery framework, which is ensuring delivery within 60 minutes.

items.statement: Fashion industry growth still slow at 10-11%, but company sees growth returning and green shoots.
items.quote: I think by our estimates, industry growth is still slower or has not recovered back to the same levels as it was a year ago. It is still in the 10%, 11% range. But we know as a combination o f various initiatives, we have taken growth in our case is definitely coming back, and we are also seeing green shoots as we head -- as we are in the first few months of this new financial year.

items.statement: Fashion business unit economics improved; with higher scale, more controlled burn, moving faster towards profitability.
items.quote: So with higher scale, I think we are looking at overall just more controlled burn. So we'll just continue to move faster towards profitability with better growth coming on board. On the gross margin side, flowing down to the contribution margin side, you've seen significant improvement.

items.statement: Fashion business will continue to improve EBITDA successively due to healthy unit economics.
items.quote: So healthy unit economics, in summary, will mean that we will continue to get better on EBITDA successively for the fashion business.

items.statement: eB2B business needs investment for a few more years before profitability; long-term guidance to be updated.
items.quote: We have to invest for a few more years before it gets to profitability. We've given that long-term guidance last year, and we'll update that again this year.

items.statement: Working capital days reduced to 34 from 42; ROCE now double digits at 11.3%.
items.quote: So this is reflected in the form of working capital days coming down to 34 from 42 a year back and with ROCE now in double digits and going up to 11.3%.

items.statement: Operating cash flow at INR467 crores; surplus cash after lease payments and capex.
items.quote: So the operating cash flow now stands at INR467 crores. And what I would like to also point out is after lease payments as well as capex, there is still a significant amount of surplus cash.

items.statement: NCLT approval received for merger and demerger schemes; no impact on consolidated financials.
items.quote: We would like to update all of you that in May 2025, we received NCLT approval for both the schemes, which is a merger of LBB into Fashion. LBB was already 100% subsidiary of the Fashion business. The other one is a demerger of our Superstore business into Nykaa E-Retail. Both of these have received NCLT approvals and the financials now factor that in.

items.statement: Working capital currently close to a month; further improvement expected but less steep than current year.
items.quote: So we are currently very close to a month in terms of net working capital. So I would say from here, yes, obviously, there would be more and more improvement opportunities, but unlikely to be as steep as what you have seen in the current year.

items.statement: Beauty multi-brand retail has scope to improve marketing income via more advertising opportunities.
items.quote: So even if I look at the main business, which is the beauty multi-brand retailing business, there is scope to continue to improve marketing income by creating more advertising opportunities on our platform, which we have been doing over the past several quarters.

items.statement: Own brands and eB2B have room to improve margins as they mature and improve mix.
items.quote: And then when I look at our own brands as well as our B2B, eB2B business there, as we've said in the past, we're still not where we want to be in terms of margin. And that will come as those businesses get a bit more mature and as they get to a better mix in terms of repeat versus new customers, and they continue to bring, as you can see on this slide, eB2B is continuing every year to bring its fu

items.statement: Price-based competition in beauty may recur; difficult to predict if behind us.
items.quote: So it's difficult to give you a definitive answer whether this is behind us. It seems to be for now, but you never know. It can come up at any t ime.

items.statement: Nykaa Now uses dark stores, not physical stores, for fulfillment.
items.quote: So yes, I think to FN' s point, Nykaa Now is being done in a more traditional rapid delivery quick commerce type model, which is to leverage the dark store concept or as we call it the micro fulfillment centers.

items.statement: Physical stores used for hyperlocal delivery predominantly for luxury products.
items.quote: So that capability exists. We do use it, and it is used predominantly f or luxury products.

items.statement: FY26 cost-to-income ratio target for Nuvama Wealth is 100 basis points lower than FY25 full-year level
items.quote: For FY '26, I think we are actually looking at 100 basis points down.

items.statement: FY26 net new money target for Nuvama Private ARR assets is INR10,000-11,000 crores (25-30% on INR44,000 crores base)
items.quote: If we are able to do anywhere between 25-30% on that, so you are again looking at INR10,000 crores to INR11,000 crores coming from there is what we will target.

items.statement: FY26 net new money target for Nuvama Wealth MPIS assets is INR7,000-8,000 crores (25-30% on INR30,000 crores base)
items.quote: Similarly, on the Wealth side, now our MPIS book would be around maybe INR30,000 crores, again, a 25-30%, so maybe INR7,000 - 8,000 crores there.

items.statement: FY26 Asset Management net new money target is INR5,000-6,000 crores (CRE INR2,000-2,300 cr, public markets INR3,000-4,000 cr, private markets INR800-1,000 cr)
items.quote: So, if you add all this together, we are again order of magnitude INR5,000 - 6,000 crores.

items.statement: FY26 total core net new money target across Private, Wealth and Asset Management is INR23,000-24,000 crores minimum
items.quote: So, if I add all this together, we come back to some INR23,000 - 24,000 crores at the bare minimum is what we target.

items.statement: FY26 lending book growth target is INR1,800-2,000 crores net increase on opening book of ~INR5,000 crores
items.quote: So, by end of year, it should have grown by INR1,800-2,000 crores is what ideally we would want to target.

items.statement: Steady-state lending yield target is 5-5.5% for Wealth and 4.5-5% for Private
items.quote: I think the steady state for our Wealth business would be anywhere between 5-5.5% and for our Private business would be again between 4.5-5%.

items.statement: Asset Management business expected to breakeven quarterly around mid-FY27 at ~INR20,000 crores AUM
items.quote: I think FY '27 somewhere around the middle is when we should start seeing that business breakeven on a quarterly basis.

items.statement: Opex growth expected to remain around 10% year-on-year in FY26 similar to FY25
items.quote: I think we will be in the similar ZIP code in terms of opex growth year-on-year. So close to 10% seems reasonable, and that's our expectation.

items.statement: Asset Services pipeline extremely strong after F&O regulatory uncertainty removed; expecting decent growth on elevated base
items.quote: So subsequent to this change, the amount of interest that has started to come back again, most of the people who were sitting on the fence are coming back. So, I think we should see a good year once again.

items.statement: Clearing business yield new normal expected at 1.8-1.9% (vs 1.61% FY25) assuming some FD yield decline in H2
items.quote: So actually, clearing business, I think the new normal should be closer to maybe 1.8-1.9%.

items.statement: Management sees 'madness' in market hiring and compensation; warns many firms will get decimated when cycle turns
items.quote: I mean, I think in a sense, there's some sort of madness happening in the market right now, the way people are building out teams and the way compensation has been dea lt, I don't know, it looks like a race to

items.statement: Private credit fund team being finalized; target launch by Q3 or Q4 FY26
items.quote: We are in the process of identifying and closing the team, and maybe by Q3 or Q4, we should be up and running with that.

items.statement: Commercial real estate fund at INR1,700 crores first close; targeting INR4,000 crores in next 2-3 quarters; first deployment done in Delhi office asset >INR460 cr equity value
items.quote: The next phase will be to take this fund from current INR1,700 crores to INR4,000 crores in maybe next two to three quarters.

items.statement: Internal target to reach 14% margin.
items.quote: So I think considering these one -off issues and also the additional margin, fixed cost leverage that's going to come up with the tubular battery being operational, while I have mentioned earlier also that at this lead level,, while 13% kind of a margin is what we have seen earlier, our internal target is definitely to reach our originally stated position of 14% margin.

items.statement: FY26 capex similar to FY25.
items.quote: For FY '26, we may have to spend a capex of a similar amount as what we have spent during the current year.

items.statement: New Energy Business capex around INR1,000 crores for FY26.
items.quote: But I think New Energy Business would require at least INR1,000 crores capex for the FY '26.

items.statement: Took 2% price increase in April.
items.quote: We have taken a price increase in the month of April to mitigate some of these cost numbers.

items.statement: Cost headwinds may persist for at least a couple of quarters.
items.quote: So this should help us in the coming quarters to improve our margins, while some of these headwinds on costs may persist for at least a couple of quarters.

items.statement: Tubular battery plant commercial production starting in June.
items.quote: The tubular battery plant reinstatement is underway with commercial production starting in June, allowing us to put our own manufactured products into the market with less reliance on trading.

items.statement: 4-wheeler OEM growth flattish, uptick expected in Q2.
items.quote: We are seeing the volume projections to be a bit flattish, but we expect that during Q2, there could be some uptick in the volumes.

items.statement: 2-wheeler OEM demand down in Q1, uptick expected next quarter.
items.quote: As far as 2-wheeler is concerned, yes, Q1 of this financial year has been a little and the volumes are on a downward trajectory. We hope that there will be an uptick in the OEM demand in the next quarter.

items.statement: US tariffs causing wait-and-watch, changes in order flow.
items.quote: So we are seeing some changes in the order flow from some of our U.S. customers. But the larger impact possibly could be if countries have differential duties, I mean, if for example, if India were to have a lower duty structure as against, let's say, some country in Southeast Asia, then obviously, their capacities in order to fill, they may start looking at elsewhere market.

items.statement: Antimony prices have gone up, no supply constraint.
items.quote: No, there is no supply constraint per se, but definitely, the prices have gone up. We are able to source the material that is required for our production, but the prices have definitely have gone

items.statement: First gigafactory capacity coming online in first half of 2027.
items.quote: We broke ground earlier this year on our first gigafactory that should see capacity coming online around in the first half of 2027.

items.statement: First phase of New Energy Business requires INR2,000-2,500 crores, to be met from internal cash flow and some leverage.
items.quote: From our cash flow management point of view, we believe the first phase would require in the New Energy Business close to INR2,000 crores to INR2,500 crores, which we believe we can easily meet with our existing lead acid business cash flow generation, maybe some bit of leverage that we have to take on the balance sheet of the holding company.

items.statement: EBITDA of $4-5 per kWh possible if $20-25 per kWh over material cost, needs 8-10 GWh capacity.
items.quote: Raghu, as I mentioned earlier also, I think, however, if we are able to get over and above the material cost, if we are able to get $20 to $25 per kilowatt hour, then I'm sure an EBITDA of $4 to $5 is possible. That is something much will depend on the sca le efficiency. At this point of time, we believe, as I mentioned earlier as well, considering the current capex costs that are coming in and th

items.statement: LFP cell prices around $55 per kWh, NMC around $60, downward trend.
items.quote: I think LFP, we have seen the best price in some cases was seen around $50 per kilowatt hour, but it is still around that $55. But we have also seen based on the import data, one-off case where there was even sub-$50 level as well. NMC, I think considering the lower quantity that we are buying, it is still around $60 or so. But both are on a downward trajectory, at least in the last two, three qua

items.statement: Trading revenue about 15% of total revenue.
items.quote: About 15% of the revenue is from trading.

items.statement: Store additions to be higher next year, maintaining 80-20 franchise-COCO ratio.
items.quote: It should be a little higher going forward, Videesha, right now as we look at it, right? Obviously, as I mentioned, we would want to continue. And we've largely retained, which is about an 80-20 ratio between franchise and COCO. But it should be a little higher next year compared to the previous year that we've seen.

items.statement: Floatz revenue expected around INR200 crores this year if momentum continues.
items.quote: And this year, my sense is if this continues momentum, right, we should be in the range of about INR200 crores.

items.statement: Zero Base Merchandising to cover about 300 stores by December end, 45-50% of retail turnover.
items.quote: So, my sense is that we should be covering about, ideally, my best guess is about 300-odd stores by [December] end. And that should cover us -- my sense is about 50% or 45% of our turnover on retail.

items.statement: Largest ever backend capex installed at Batanagar for PUDIP machine.
items.quote: We installed our largest ever capex in the back end in Batanagar in the PUDIP machine. This backs our commercialization of the IMEVA machine that we did last year.

items.statement: Gross margin erosion of 230 bps year-on-year due to mix and value proposition.
items.quote: The gross margin were at about INR455 crores, while there is an erosion of about 230 bps versus the last year same quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA margin reported at 25.5%, like-to-like 23.5% due to accounting change.
items.quote: EBITDA margin reported is at about 25.5%. The change versus last year is about 14 bps lower. Now in the EBITDA margin, there is a change in accounting for one of the licensed brands based on the Ind AS. Like-to-like EBITDA margin versus last year would have been about 23.5%.

items.statement: Resetting cost structure for lead products to offset value proposition impact.
items.quote: But also, the fact that we have been consciously providing value proposition, while we are parallelly working towards resetting the cost structure for some of our lead products like the kind of example that I mentioned, Sameer, in my presentation. And that should pan out over the next -- so both of these are the things that have contributed to the gross margin that you see.

items.statement: Demand conditions tight; focus on value and presentation to drive performance.
items.quote: Yes, yes. No. So obviously, we know that the demand conditions are -- have been tight, Gaurav. However, within that, what we see is that our ability to do 2, 3 things, right? One is provide the right kind of portfolio to consumers, which we are looking for, and many of them are what we see very clearly are looking for some kind of a relief from the overall inflation that they've seen and, therefor

items.statement: Floatz continues 40%+ growth, doubled in 2 years, premiumized pricing.
items.quote: It is also -- continues its growth rate of almost 40% plus. As you can see out here, it's almost more than doubled in the last 2 years backed by solid volumes.

items.statement: Power portfolio expanding with EasySlide to 1,200 doors and Stamina+ to 400 doors.
items.quote: Now we are taking it to 1,200 doors. We are also resetting the price point on this to make it even more attractive. And also, the Stamina+ collection, which is at a premium end at about INR4,000 MRP. And that has shown some good results in the first launch in the last quarter, and that's been taken to almost 400 doors.

items.statement: Employee cost higher by 100 bps this quarter, non-recurring.
items.quote: In terms of percentage of revenue, it has marginally gone up by 30 basis points, which also includes one exception -- one-off exceptions of about, let's say, 100 basis points in terms of my employee cost. Gunjan Shah: It should not be recurring

items.statement: Inventory reduced 16% over 5 quarters, aged inventory down 30-35%.
items.quote: The inventory is a significant drop at 16%. This is over a continuing drop over the last almost now 5 quarters that we have managed to do. That has shown up in terms of turns also. We still see some more meat going forward on this entire piece, not only in total quantity, but also on the quality of inventory, which is what you see in the aged inventory that's about 30% to 35% lower.

items.statement: Volume growth mid-single digits in Q4, broad-based.
items.quote: We don't share that. But as I've mentioned in my press release also as well as my commentary in the start, the second quarter that we've seen reasonably broad-based volume growth in the mid-single digits would be the best.

items.statement: Franchise stores at 625, expansion in urbanizing India.
items.quote: Now franchise stores stand at about 625. For the first time after a long time, we have started seeing some revival and contribution from the less than INR1,000 price point, which shows up in our volume growth, though we would have desired much more, so that we can also result that into revenue growth, which we are hopeful for going forward.

items.statement: Customer First transformation project launched with external partner for consumer centricity.
items.quote: We have launched off a large transformation project with an external partner on what we call is Customer First, on how are we able to make sure that everything that we are doing through the organization comes through the value chain and impacts the consumer.

items.statement: Distillery capacity utilization expected to continue at 90% to 95%.
items.quote: We are currently running at about 90% plus capacity utilization. We expect that to continue, and our endeavor is to move the needle substantially up because the benefit is there in utilizing our assets efficiently, and we have an opportunity unlike the sugar business. So 90% to 95% is the kind of capacity utilization we are looking at.

items.statement: Consumer products business aims to beat 12% annual growth of branded packaged food in India.
items.quote: Branded packaged food business in India is growing at about 12% annually. We will be trying to beat that estimate in terms of our growth rates, and we will continue to keep focused on building the brand and driving the distribution.

items.statement: Refinery run rate to increase due to better white premiums than FY25.
items.quote: So we are seeing the white premiums going back, may not be up to the levels that what we witnessed in FY '24, but definitely much better than the FY '25 level. So that will increase the run rate of the refining operation.

items.statement: Sugar MSP should be in early 40s for meaningful viability.
items.quote: I would say something into the early 40s would only be near meaningful. However, it still continues to be a deliberation with them on the MSP.

items.statement: Risk of sugar price decline with higher production and limited ethanol impetus.
items.quote: Yes, with more sugar coming into the balance and with these kinds of release quotas and sugarcane ethanol not being given as much of an impetus, there is certainly a risk of downward sliding of prices.

items.statement: Concern over potential lifting of curbs on U.S. ethanol imports negatively impacting industry.
items.quote: We are also concerned, I will say, by the fact that there are conversations as part of a broader U.S.-India trade discussions that the lifting of curbs on import of U.S. ethanol is being considered. We don't know the outcome yet, but I think the industry body has officially also expressed their concern on this matter to policymakers across the board.

items.statement: Neutral outlook on cane availability with positive base due to good monsoons.
items.quote: Current timely monsoons in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu is giving us a lot of comfort. We are still in the stage of planting. Probably by the end of next quarter, we'll have a good view of any upsides that could be there. Currently, we are holding a neutral outlook with a positive base.

items.statement: Dynamic decision on ethanol vs ENA based on profitability; honor OMC commitments.
items.quote: As far as the composition of ethanol and ENA is concerned, we'll be dynamically deciding it, which is more lucrative, okay? As far as the ethanol is concerned, to the extent of the OMC commitment, we'll be honoring it. So, balance, we will be diverting into the ENA.

items.statement: No plans to enter organic or chemical-free staples currently.
items.quote: As of now, we are present in the conventional staples business, and we don't have any plans right now to enter the organic or chemical-free staples at this point in time. Maybe in at some future situation, we'll consider it.

items.statement: No specific crushing guidance for FY26; will update in September.
items.quote: Ritwik normally, we will not tell about the future, but as was Ashiq mentioning that this time, the monsoon is good. But we can come back to you may be in the September or something, what should be the probable crushing.

items.statement: Impairment taken due to poor financial performance; infusion to strengthen net worth and reduce debt.
items.quote: The impairment has been done on account of poor financial performance. I think that was looked at, and I think we were required to take that impairment. In terms of the infusion, it is to strengthen the net worth of the company and also bring about some debt reduction.

items.statement: Sugar (Control) Order does not affect refinery as it is export-oriented.
items.quote: The Sugar (Control) Order is basically for governing the domestic production, as refinery is entirely on export. So either the imports is through an advanced license or through special economic zone, these do not come under the Control Order. So we are not affected..

items.statement: Ethanol blending at 18%; auto industry prepared for 20% blend.
items.quote: In terms of the blend, I think we're up to about 18% right now. And the auto industry also is seemingly prepared for up to a 20% blend.

items.statement: No increase in molasses-based ethanol prices for almost 3 years, challenging industry margins.
items.quote: So that is a challenge, given FRPs goes up consistently every year. And last year, they actually went up by 8%. So this is what has challenged the industry and also brought EBITDA margins down significantly on the back of recently concluded capex programs.

items.statement: E-beam plant expected to generate annual revenue from two products.
items.value: INR 500 crores to INR600 crores per year
items.quote: We expect the pl an to generate revenue when it is in full steam of about INR 500 crores to INR600 crores per year from these 2 products.

items.statement: Remaining capex from announced plan to be spent this fiscal; projects to close by fiscal end.
items.quote: The remaining part will be spent in the current year. Most of it -- so all those projects should get closed by the end of this fiscal.

items.statement: Reinstatement capex of about INR40-50 crores to be spent.
items.quote: Additionally, always, there is a reinstatement capex of about INR40 crores, INR 50 crores. So that is something that will be spent.

items.statement: Hopeful of decent business from BharatNet winners in current and next years.
items.quote: However, many of the winners across the 16 circles, have used our manufacturers authorization to place their bids so we are in discussion with many of those winners, and we are hopeful of a decent level of business in the current and the next years.

items.statement: Prices changed by 3% effective yesterday.
items.quote: Effective yesterday, prices have changed by 3%.

items.statement: Net cost impact in FY25 was about 12.5% to 13%.
items.quote: So net impact, I think costs would have gone up about 12.5% to 13%.

items.statement: Expect demand revival in second half of current fiscal and growth next year.
items.quote: I think you should see growth next year for sure and probably from the second half of this year.

items.statement: Expect gradual margin improvement; most margin pressure issues behind.
items.quote: I would say that there should be gradual improvement. I think if you look at our numbers over the last 5, 6 years, this '24, '25 w as probably the first year when the margins have taken a dip and then come back to -- and not yet come back to where it was, but going towards that.

items.statement: Project sales mix increased by 8-10% over three years.
items.quote: That would have changed maybe between -- about the 8% to 10%, that would be a shift.

items.statement: Fiber capacity to increase from 4 million to 6 million kilometers after commissioning.
items.quote: So when that is done, fiber capacity will go up from the current 4 million kilometers to 6 million kilometers.

items.statement: Preform production trials to start this month; product available after 2-3 months.
items.quote: We are waiting for the production trials to start that is slated for sometime this month. When that is over, then that should take about 2 to 3 months before the trials are over and the plant stabilizes.

items.statement: OFC utilization levels expected to improve in current and next fiscal.
items.quote: So I think the utilization levels will improve in the current and the next fiscal for sure.

items.statement: Fiber prices firmed up to about $3.5 from $2.5.
items.quote: So we are seeing prices firming up now. So it's closer to $3.5 right now as opposed to $2.5, which was prevail ing for most of the year last year.

items.statement: Preform utilization expected to ramp up to 60-70% from second year.
items.quote: But from the second year onwards, I expect at least a ramp-up to initially 60%, 70%.

items.statement: EHV projects have long gestation of 12-24 months, spreading sales recognition.
items.quote: Each project takes anywhere between 12 to 24 months to complete. So your sales recognition is not at one point in time, it spreads over 24 months.

items.statement: E-beam cables for solar industry expected to grow with government targets.
items.quote: We have launched them in February, and we have recently got our certifications through BIS also. And we expect this industry to grow.

items.statement: Blended margin of around 35% for the entire year.
items.quote: For the margin, you can take a blended margin of around 35% for the entire year.

items.statement: Targeting day rates in the 60s or higher in coming tenders.
items.quote: So definitely, that's not the new range. We will be -- still be targeting the 60s or higher in the coming tenders.

items.statement: Revenue for FY27, FY28, FY29 expected in line with FY25 or FY26.
items.quote: And consequently, we expect subject to getting good rates, the revenue for FY '27, '28, '29 to be in line with whatever we have done in FY '25 or FY '26.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR1,791 crores.
items.quote: Order book position has been updated with the new contract of Jindal Explorer also being included. Order book stands at INR1,791 crores.

items.statement: No debt required to fund Jindal Pioneer acquisition; will use internal accruals.
items.quote: Going forward, we expect net cash position to improve further and it is on the basis of the internal accruals that we will generate that we will be able to discharge purchase consideration of Jindal Pioneer. There will be no requirement of any debt to fund that acquisition.

items.statement: Record revenue and profits expected in FY26.
items.quote: We have done really well over the past 2 years, and we will see record revenue and profits in FY '26.

items.statement: New contracts expected at higher rates; 35,000 one-off.
items.quote: Next contract is scheduled to be awarded towards the later part of the year after the tender comes out. We don't expect rates of 35,000 going forward. It is a one -off due to some special situations which was in place. That situation will not continue going forward.

items.statement: ONGC demand expected to increase substantially next year after BP meetings.
items.quote: And going forward, right now, ONGC , their demand is less. That's why they're coming out with less tenders because they are having some meetings with BP to streamline their process. Once that's done by the next -- the coming year, their demand would increase substantially.

items.statement: Jindal Explorer under refurbishment, expected redeployment in November or earlier.
items.quote: Correct. So, Jindal Explorer is under refurbishment as we speak. It is expected to be redeployed on the new contract in Nov ember or maybe a little earlier.

items.statement: Refurbishment for ONGC rigs usually 5 to 6 months.
items.quote: For rigs that are expected to be deployed with ONGC, refurbishment is usually 5 to 6 months. And that is also the time which is given by ONGC.

items.statement: Effective tax rate lower than 25% due to accelerated depreciation from rig acquisition.
items.quote: It will be lower than 25% because we've acquired the rig. And I'm talking about the current tax rate only. It is likely to be -- it will be lower than 25% because we have acquired the rig and we get accelerated depreciation.

items.statement: Jindal Pioneer acquisition payment to be completed within 1 year.
items.quote: It's a deferred payment schedule. The entire payment will be completed within 1 year.

items.statement: Debt will continue to reduce aggressively; net cash position.
items.quote: Yes, I've already said that. Debt will continue to reduce aggressively. And we are net cash right now. So the debt is only at a gross level.

items.statement: No plans for consolidation of Explorer and Virtue 1 in near future.
items.quote: No, I don't think so we have any such plans in the near future. But yes, the consolidation is always there in the mind, but I don't have any time lines for that.

items.statement: Looking at diversification opportunities in related services and assets.
items.quote: No. We are not only doing -- we are not only going to be th ere with the rigs offshore. We are looking at different opportunities. We are already in the space of directional drilling and mud logging. We are looking at different related services as well.

items.statement: Expects AUM mix to shift to 70% retail and 30% term loans over the next few quarters.
items.quote: So you will see the split hopefully changing to 70/30, where 70% over the next few quarters will end up being more retail, and 30% will be on the side of term loans.

items.statement: Current AUM split is about 60% term loans and 40% retail loans.
items.quote: If you see today, we almost have a 60/40 split, where there's a 60% weightage towards term loans and almost a 40% weightage towards retail loans.

items.statement: Cost of capital ranges 10 to 13-14%, blended sub 12%; term loan XIRR usually 16-17% and upwards.
items.quote: So typically, our cost of capital is fairly varied. It goes anywhere between 10 to 13-14%. From a blended perspective, our cost of capital must be sub 12% at this point in time. And typically when we do the term loan, from an (Extended Internal Rate of Return) XIRR perspective, everything is usually 16-17% and upwards.

items.statement: Expects good progress in quarters ahead, converting term loan exposures into BC co-lending partnerships.
items.quote: We do expect good progress to be coming as well in the quarters ahead, and there are some interesting partners that we've taken exposure on from a term loan perspective that we now will be converting to BC co-lending partnerships as well.

items.statement: Sees shoots of recovery in unsecured space and expects some rebound over next few quarters.
items.quote: Over the last couple of months or so, we are seeing shoots of recovery where now there is maybe a little bit of RBI relaxation towards the unsecured space as well, because potentially, I think it contracted more than their intended targets. So, hopefully, over the next few quarters we should start seeing some degree of rebound as well.

items.statement: Observed higher defaults and stress in certain partners' loan books across the industry.
items.quote: Across the industry, one of the trends that we did observe is that certain loan books of partners ended up having higher levels of defaults and stress than before.

items.statement: Cautious of exposures in companies with debt to equity upwards of 2.5 in this space.
items.quote: But what we've observed in this space is that debt to equity anywhere upwards of 2.5 in this space starts to look very, very heavy for the company, because a regulatory change may make their book incredibly volatile, and they may not be able to manage their debt effectively.

items.statement: AUM grew 74% year on year.
items.quote: We've grown 74% year on year.

items.statement: Debt to equity is fairly low at 0.4%.
items.quote: Our debt to equity right now is fairly low. It's only 0.4%.

items.statement: Apollo's 30+ PAR averages around 2.86% versus industry NPA around 2.4%, with Apollo NPA less than a percent.
items.quote: If we look at the rest of the industry, the average 30 PAR numbers for Apollo are around 2.86%. And even the NPA numbers on an average in the industry range to around 2.4%, and for us, it's less than a percent.

items.statement: AI voice calling is almost 10 times cheaper than call centers.
items.quote: And obviously it never gets tired, and it's almost 10 times cheaper.

items.statement: Term loans are short-term, 4 to 12 months in duration.
items.value: 4 months, 6 months, or maybe maximum 12 months
items.quote: But given that we now are first collaborating with them in the form of a short-term term loan, which may be 4 months, 6 months, or maybe maximum 12 months in duration, it allows us to get a lot of thorough diligence done.

items.statement: ROEs have always been in double digits over the last 8 years.
items.quote: One of the things that we're incredibly proud of is that, if you see our record over the last 8 years, despite it being a very young industry, our ROEs have always been in double digits.

items.statement: AUM moved from about 85 to 83, not seen as a meaningful dip.
items.quote: I think it's gone from some 85 to 83, if I have the numbers correctly, so I don't look at it as a meaningful dip either way.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of sub-20% for FY26
items.quote: So overall growth, as we mentioned in our previous call also is in the range of somewhere around sub-20%. That's the top line growth we are anticipating in current financial year '25-'26.

items.statement: Long-term revenue CAGR target of 15% over next few years
items.quote: I think the long-term plan is to consistently grow at a 15% CAGR over the next few years.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth forecast of 20% to 25%
items.quote: I think going forward in FY '26, we continue a similar between a 20% to 25% growth rate forecast for FY '26.

items.statement: Order book of INR2,275 crores with 37% for EVs and 85% for PV segment
items.quote: Looking ahead, we are pleased to report a healthy order book of INR2,275 crores. Notably, 37 % of this is dedicated to the electric vehicles and 85% is allocated to the Passenger Vehicle segment.

items.statement: 55% to 60% of order book from Maruti Suzuki and SMG combined
items.quote: That's correct, almost close to 55% to 60% is from Maruti Suzuki and SMG put together.

items.statement: More than 50% to 60% of order book to convert to SOP in FY26
items.quote: And again, a lot of these new businesses from the order book will come in, almost close to more than 50% to 60% of the order book will actually come in FY '26 as well across different manufacturing facilities.

items.statement: FY26 capex guidance of INR180-220 crores
items.quote: The guidance for FY '26 would be continuing in a similar time of approximately between INR180 crores to INR220 crores.

items.statement: No specific capex guidance for FY27 but asset turnover expected to improve
items.quote: We do not have any specific capex guidance for FY '27, but considering the massive growth, which we are building in FY '26, we do believe that the asset turnover ratios also should improve compared to FY '25 in FY '27.

items.statement: Manufacturing EBITDA margin of 9.8% in Q4 and 8.7% for full year FY25
items.quote: So, if we see our manufacturing EBITDA for the quarter 4 is at 9.8% and on a full year basis, we are at 8.7%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 9.5% to 10% for FY26
items.quote: So, you can see this kind of a margin maybe closer to about 10% or 9.5%, somewhere in this range going for the next fiscal year.

items.statement: Tooling margin guidance of 12% to 15% on sustained basis
items.quote: I would say the guidance would be that we should continue anywhere between 12% to 15% on tooling margins, which would be on a sustained basis.

items.statement: LED revenue share target of 65% for FY26
items.quote: And in FY '26, we are actually looking at probably 65% of total revenue coming from LED lighting.

items.statement: LED material margin lower than conventional but overall margin improvement expected
items.quote: Number two, I think, yes, there is a bit of a pressure on the margins because of higher LED concentration, specifically on the raw material consumption because the material margin on an LED lamp is lower, but then there are several other factors, as Ravi pointed out, where we do expect margins to become better going forward in FY '26.

items.statement: Industry outlook of 4% to 5% growth with export restriction headwinds
items.quote: So industry outlook, as I said in my commentary, if I look at the SIAM data, we're actually looking at the overall industry growth of about 4% to 5%, there are certain headwinds, particularly on the export restrictions, what China has done on the REE, which means the rare earth elements.

items.statement: Potential supply disruptions in June-July due to China rare earth export restrictions
items.quote: And as recent as last week, SIAM has put out a caution note where they say that the industry could have certain disruptions in the month of June and July.

items.statement: Chakan Phase 2 SOP scheduled for Q2 FY26 with peak revenue of INR250-300 crores in FY27
items.quote: The peak revenue from Phase 2 is expected to come in FY '27, and that would be in the range of INR250 crores to INR300 crores.

items.statement: Expects to sustain strong growth in revenue and margins in FY26.
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY ‘26, we expect to sustain strong growth in both revenue and margins, supported by our strategic diversification efforts and improvements in raw material sourcing and cost management.

items.statement: 150 KLPD ethanol expansion at Bathinda to be commissioned by December 2025.
items.quote: The work for 150 expansion at Bathinda is progressing well, with all clearances in hand, and we are hoping to commission this plant by December 2025.

items.statement: 60 TPH paddy straw boiler to be commissioned in November 2025.
items.quote: In addition, the installation of a 60 tonne per hour paddy straw boiler is in progress, which is aimed to reduce fuel costs further for our company and improve operational efficiency. We are expecting to commission this boiler in November 2025.

items.statement: 75 KLPD biodiesel plant in Bathinda expected to be commissioned in July 2025.
items.quote: Our 75 KLPD biodiesel plant in Bathinda is at an advanced stage of development, and is expected to be commissioned in July 2025.

items.statement: At 100% utilization, 75 KLPD biodiesel plant to generate INR 200-225 crores revenue.
items.quote: For the revenue figures, working at 100% capacity utilization at 75 KLPD biodiesel plant should give us around INR 200 crores to INR 225-odd crores in terms of revenue.

items.statement: 850 KLPD capacity to generate INR 2,100-2,200 crores revenue.
items.quote: So a conservative figure for 850 capacity is around INR 2,100 to INR 2,200 crores in terms of revenue.

items.statement: Additional 250 KLPD capacity to generate INR 700-750 crores revenue.
items.quote: And the next stage would be post that of 250. So that should give us at least another INR 700 crores to INR 750 crores in revenue.

items.statement: Expects distillery margins to improve in next 1-2 quarters due to lower raw material prices.
items.quote: See, for the distillery business, we are expecting that the margins for the next at least 1 or 2 quarters should improve since raw material prices are starting to stop in, thanks to the FCI rice and bumper crop for maize, especially in UP, Punjab and Bihar.

items.statement: Expects maize prices to average INR 25-25.5 for the year.
items.quote: But with the relief of surplus rice for the ethanol industry, I expect that maize prices for the entire year should average around INR 25 to INR 25.5, because as of yesterday or day before, the government has also increased the MSP for maize to INR 24 now.

items.statement: At maize price INR 24, margins improve by INR 2 per liter.
items.quote: See then margins should improve by INR 2.

items.statement: At maize price INR 25.5, margin per liter is about INR 5.
items.quote: See, with the INR 25.5 about I would say, about INR 5.

items.statement: In Q1, about 30% of processing used FCI rice.
items.quote: It is mainly from Q1 that we have started to use a little bit of FCI rice as well. About 30% of FCI rice.

items.statement: Biodiesel unit has provision to sell maize oil as industrial oil if OMC issues arise.
items.quote: And keeping that in mind, we have kept the provision in our facility that if biodiesel prices are not viable or there are some issues on the OMC front, then we can process this maize oil and sell it as an industrial oil, whether that is for the animal feed industry or other uses.

items.statement: Phased exit from edible oil business, trying to complete by June end.
items.quote: See, we are trying by June end. Let’s see.

items.statement: Expects 100% paddy straw fuel reliance by October/November 2025.
items.quote: By October or November of this year, we are hoping that we will be 100% reliant on paddy straw with the commissioning of our new boiler.

items.statement: Estimates 20% revenue dip and 30% profit dip for FY26 due to US headwinds and higher R&D.
items.quote: The company estimates a possible dip in revenue by 20% and profits by 30% due to geopolitical uncertainties and pricing pressure in its core product portfolio in the U.S. and increased R&D expenses.

items.statement: First half of FY26 to be good, second half weaker.
items.quote: I would say that the first half will be good, but second half will not be as strong as the second half. The second half will be weaker than the first half.

items.statement: Plans to spend INR300-350 crores capex per year, with total plan of INR500-600 crores over 1.5-2 years.
items.quote: Every year, we spend about INR300 crores to INR350 crores. So, we have a capex plan of about INR500 crores, INR600 crores, but per year, looks like we're going to spend about INR300 crores.

items.statement: Targets R&D spend up to INR400 crores in FY26, similar to FY25.
items.quote: I would want to spend, I think, a similar amount of money this year as well. We have some very nice projects that we have lined up and I think the really good ones are always very expensive. So , I think that's what we are trying to do. But I think we want to spend about in that range up to INR400 crores is what we're targeting.

items.statement: Expects base India business to grow 7-10%, with major launches driving higher growth.
items.quote: I think of the publicly announced pipeline, I think the base business should grow around 7% to 10%. But I think the 2 major launches that will drive the growth.

items.statement: Plans to file 7-8 products in US.
items.quote: 7 to 8 is what we're targeting to file

items.statement: Expects Agro business to break even in FY26 with revenue of INR160-170 crores.
items.quote: I think this year, we feel we are going to hit that critical mass where we'll start breaking even. We are doing about INR60 crores net revenue last year. So , I think we need to hit about INR160 crores to INR170 crores at least to have that EBITDA positive.

items.statement: Plans to close an acquisition in FY26.
items.quote: We are looking at acquisitions. We are looking at a lot of active acquisitions. I think I'm positive that we'll be able to close something in this financial year, that's the idea.

items.statement: Expects Semaglutide launch by end of FY26.
items.quote: Semaglutide, which we're expecting maybe end of the financial year.

items.statement: Expects Risdiplam order in July-August, launch immediately if favorable.
items.quote: July, August, we should expect some order on that. Right now, we have not launched the product. We're waiting for the clarity from the 2 Judge bench and then based on that, we'll strategize what to do.

items.statement: Non-US formulation exports estimated at INR800-900 crores.
items.quote: Ex of U.S. So, I would say about INR800 crores to INR900 crores minus U.S.

items.statement: NCE R&D spend estimated at INR25-30 crores in FY26.
items.quote: the NCE will probably see about, INR25 crores to INR30 crores, I would estimate in that amount roughly.

items.statement: No guidance for FY27 margins due to moving parts.
items.quote: At this time, no, Bino. It's hard to predict anything right now because there's so many moving parts.

items.statement: Management not comfortable giving ROE estimate for FY26; expects MFI portfolio to stabilize before growth resumes in Q3/Q4 FY26
items.quote: I do not think I am comfortable giving an estimate at this point.

items.statement: Consolidated profitability expected to continue; MFI subsidiary expected to be independently profitable by Q2 FY26
items.quote: Honestly, by Q2, we are expecting even micro to be independently profitable. But I mean, do not hold me to that. We are trying our best. At consol level, we should continue to remain profitable.

items.statement: New credit and recovery structure to add at least 1% to overall OPEX; 160 BCMs hired plus 30 management and 600 recovery officers
items.quote: As far as operating cost is concerned, we expect this to add it, I mean, the new recovery function and credit function to add at least 1% to the OPEX overall, that was our initial estimate.

items.statement: CGFMU premium ~1% of portfolio outstanding per year (~1.6-1.75% over average 2-year tenor); expected to be offset by lower credit costs
items.quote: So, it's about 1% of the portfolio outstanding of the custom per year. So that should come out to be about 1.6% or 1.75% for the life of the customer, the average loan tenor is two years only.

items.statement: MFI disbursements declined 26% YoY in Q4 FY25; April-May FY26 disbursements slow, zero DPD stabilized but not improving; MSME disbursements grew 20% YoY in FY25
items.quote: April and May have been quite slow for industry, so disbursements have come down quite a bit. Zero DPD buckets have stabilized but are not improving overall.

items.statement: Standalone AUM (MSME, micro-LAP, 2W) grew 25% YoY to Rs 560 cr, now ~25% of consolidated AUM; MFI AUM declined 23% YoY to Rs 1,686 cr
items.quote: As of March 31st, 2025, standalone AUM stood at Rs. 560 crores, registering a year-on-year growth of 25 %. Disbursement in FY '25 was Rs. 481 crores, up 20% compared to FY '24.

items.statement: MFI gross NPA improved to 3.37% (down 75 bps from Dec 2024); Stage-2 assets Rs 85 cr with Rs 38 cr provision; 34% of MFI AUM under CGFMU (75% coverage)
items.quote: As of 31st March 2025, our gross non-performing assets stood at 3.37%, representing an improvement of 75 basis points from 4.13% in December 2024.

items.statement: MFI zero DPD collection efficiency improved from 97.3% (Nov 2024) to 98.8% (Mar 2025); PAR 1-30 ~18%; attrition ~62-63% in MFI, target 40% by H1 FY26
items.quote: For the MFI book, zero bucket collection efficiency for the quarter stood at about 98.5% and improved to 98.8% in March 2025.

items.statement: Stress concentrated in Rajasthan and parts of Gujarat; Maharashtra, MP, UP, Bihar showing improvement; Karnataka exposure <1%
items.quote: I mean, honestly, that changes. Every state seems to be taking its own turn. So if you were to ask me right now, it's probably Rajasthan. I mean, Maharashtra is showing significant improvement, s o is MP. Certain areas of Gujarat have trouble , eastern Gujarat side

items.statement: ARC transaction in Mar 2025: Rs 185 cr assets sold for Rs 36.75 cr (15% cash, 85% SRs); 95% written off in FY25; quarterly SR valuation required
items.quote: The transaction has happened on 28th of March, so Rs. 36.75 crores is the mark to market kind of value.

items.statement: Cost of borrowings stable; marginal cost down 25-50 bps over last 6 months; MCLR not yet reduced by banks despite repo cuts
items.quote: Generally stable, Amit. In fact, the marginal cost of borrowing for the last six months has incrementally kind of come down only by about 25 to 50 basis points.

items.statement: New credit structure (BCM model) implemented in 140 of 391 branches; full rollout by Q2 FY26; early delinquency 3x lower in BCM-originated loans
items.quote: Currently, we have implemented the new credit structure in about 140 of our 391 branches, with the remaining branches to be implemented by Q2 of FY '26. Early indicators in asset quality for loans originated under the new credit structure are quite encouraging.

items.statement: MFI customers with 3+ lenders ~23% (down from 26-27% in Sep 2024); daily credit bureau reporting; voter ID primary KYC for bureau
items.quote: I think three plus would be about 23%, I think it would have come down to 23%. So that's probably a close answer.

items.statement: MSME zero DPD collection efficiency 99.5% in Mar 2025; gross NPA 3.38%; digital collections 20-25% (up to 35-40% in some districts)
items.quote: March zero DPD collection efficiency in MSME portfolio was 99.5% and 99% plus for the quarter as a whole.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM Rs 2,245 cr (down 15% YoY); debt-equity 1.3x; surplus liquidity Rs 269 cr; CAR 37.34% (standalone), 48.37% (Namra)
items.quote: Our consolidated balance sheet remains strong, supported by healthy debt equity ratio of 1.3x and surplus liquidity of Rs. 269 crores.

items.statement: Revenue will increase in FY26 as recently opened resorts mature; EBITDA margin expected to improve from ~34-35% toward 40% target over project life
items.quote: So, the more lucrative and more incremental EBITDA margin you will find in '26. As well as, in terms of turnover also you will find a major chunk of incremental revenue in top line.

items.statement: ~Rs 100 crore of work-in-progress will convert to fixed assets in FY26; additional Rs 30-40 crore needed to finish 4-5 current resorts
items.quote: Major way we have invested CAPEX, in Thinnakara there is 200 rooms. So, this year, our work in progress will convert into development around Rs. 100 crores, approximately Rs. 100 crores, and work in progress goes to the fixed assets.

items.statement: Additional Rs 30-40 crore capex required to complete 4-5 ongoing resort projects
items.quote: Okay. Rs. 30 crores to Rs. 40 crores, approximately I am saying, but it's Rs. 30 crores to Rs. 40 crores to finish present four, five resorts.

items.statement: Six resorts under development including Serengeti (25 rooms), Thinnakara-II (200 rooms), Kashid/Kihim (~35-40 rooms), Jaisalmer (40-50 rooms); two near completion
items.quote: Exactly. Out of that, I have explained the status of these six resorts is under progress as well as ready to progress, ready to start with development process.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin ~34% in FY25 vs 35% in FY24; pressure from new resort openings; target 40% average EBITDA margin over project life
items.quote: It's a 35% EBITDA margin in last year. This year is 34% EBITDA margin in consolidated.

items.statement: Lease/rent cost ~Rs 16 crore in FY25 (~10% of revenue); no debt; promoter group may contribute funds if needed
items.quote: Rs. 16 crores. This year we paid about Rs. 16 crores rent, total. So, it's about you can understand 10% of the total revenue.

items.statement: Strong demand for experiential luxury travel in Tier 2/3 cities and international destinations like Serengeti and Lakshadweep; ARR per room higher internationally
items.quote: We want to work only in experiential hospitalities, beautiful, scenic, rivers, seashores, jungles, like that places were we can give more experience to my tourists, my guests, that is the basic purpose.

items.statement: Shift toward high-ARR experiential resorts (Jawai, Lakshadweep, Serengeti) and asset-light development-management model; 775+ rooms across 15 resorts + 1 hotel
items.quote: We are in some different kind of models that we are working on it. And in terms of total Vision '28, we are further acquiring more properties, more locations, which you will get a good location ideology of the Praveg.

items.statement: Seasonal occupancy variations (summer low at Jawai), Kumbh Mela diverted tourists in Q4 FY25, government bookings block inventory impacting ARR strategy
items.quote: Last quarter there was a major boom at Kumbh. Kumbh marketing was all we are knowing, all the public was diverted to Kumbh. So, it affected other property for tourist also.

items.statement: Debt-free; funded via internal accruals, warrants, and asset-light development-management model where landowner funds capex; promoter group may contribute if needed
items.quote: We are a debt-free company right now. We do not want to raise any debt. That is our strategy.

items.statement: International expansion progressing: Serengeti (25 rooms) received environment clearance; pursuing Masai Mara; international ARR expected higher than domestic
items.quote: Serengeti, we have just two days before got environment clearance, that is the final certification for that project. And the project team is working on it.

items.statement: Advertising segment growing via smart-toilet/hoarding model: acquired Abhik & Bidhan; won contracts in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Goa; revenue up 80-90% YoY in first year
items.quote: Sir, you can see this first year of revenue, that's incremental around 80%, 90% of the last year's revenue. That journey will be continued until we get a good acquisition, until we get good market support, we will do it.

items.statement: Strategic alliances: Mahindra Holidays (80 rooms bulk inventory, no fee), IHCL SeleQtions/Ginger (management fee minor, industry standard, confidential)
items.quote: Mahindra is not taking any money from us, any charges from us. Mahindra is giving a contribution to us in terms of sales, number one.

items.statement: Lakshadweep access improved: flights increased from 1 to 4 (7 planned); permit process simplified — Praveg issues guest vouchers, handles backend
items.quote: Before this resort started there was one flight in all, now there are already four flights in operation. Apart from that, another three flights is getting added by the government of India, so there will be total seven flights.

items.statement: Daman cluster performing above expectations; Tripadvisor Travelers' Choice Award 2025; near-full occupancy with Mahindra guests; new Kachigam property launched for weddings
items.quote: Sir, it's amazing. It's over than our expectation. After our own guests as well as Mahindra Group guests is making almost full status of occupancy.

items.statement: FY26 performance expected to be better than last year despite Gagillapur slowdown.
items.quote: We cannot give you any guidance on this, but definitely all I can say is it's going to be better than last year. And I also want to make it clear that the slowdown on operation in Gagillapur will continue for a quarter or two.

items.statement: FY26 capex estimate is Rs. 600 crores, including Granules Life Science, oncology, and peptide investments.
items.quote: So currently, we have done estimate for FY '26, FY '27 we are still working on. So FY '26, overall CAPEX estimate is about Rs. 600 crores. This includes further CAPEX, which we have to incur for Granules Life Science and also oncology and peptide investment.

items.statement: Senn Chemicals investment is on top of FY26 capex, with enterprise value of Rs. 450 crores.
items.quote: Yes, you are right, Senn Chemical investment is on top of that. That is equity plus debt put together, Rs. 450 crores Enterprise Value and we did that recently.

items.statement: API and PFI share expected to remain around 25% as focus shifts to formulations.
items.quote: Yes, currently it is less than 25% and this is how the trend also we see going forward, as Chairman clarified in the earlier conversation. So we are producing API more for in -house consumption. So we are focusing more on formulation. So this trend of aroun d close to 25% of API, PFI will be in that range

items.statement: Tariffs may lead to price increases; company cannot absorb them.
items.quote: We are talking to all our customers in the US about the possible impact. And we have been mentioning that if duties, tariffs come in, we will have to increase prices, there is no way we can absorb it.

items.statement: Gagillapur remediation expenses to continue in Q1 and Q2, gradually declining.
items.quote: It will continue for Q1 and Q2, but slowly declining. But definitely till Q2 we see that it should be continuing. We have taken up a complete remediation plan, not a mandatory part exercise.

items.statement: Oncology portfolio expected to start generating revenues from FY28 onwards.
items.quote: So overall, this is the portfolio, and we expect this portfolio to start yielding us revenues from FY '28 onwards.

items.statement: Granules Life Science capacity utilization expected at 40-50% this year and 90% by next fiscal end.
items.quote: Once we get this approval, we will start full production and then I think by possibly this year, we may do about 40%, 50% capacity utilization and close to 90% by next fiscal end.

items.statement: Senn Chemicals expected to remain breakeven or slight loss for next one to three quarters.
items.quote: It's sort of breakeven or slight loss as of today, yes. And we think in the next one or two quarters or three quarters it will continue to be around that level, but going forward with the new strategy, it should improve.

items.statement: Senn Chemicals current annual sales approximately CHF20 million.
items.quote: So currently, they are doing roughly CHF20 million a year and with the breakeven EBITDA. And they are largely into CDMO related to peptides, pharma, cosmetics and theragnostics.

items.statement: Professional expenses including air freight and US FDA consultancy were close to Rs. 60 crores in FY25.
items.quote: So, I will just quantify not only professional expenses, all kinds of expenses, including air freight and US FDA consultancy expenses, all have been close to Rs. 60 crores for FY '25.

items.statement: R&D expenses for FY25 were Rs. 2,377 million; will continue spending in coming quarters.
items.quote: R&D expenses for the year was Rs. 2,377 million. We are going to continue to spend on R&D in the coming quarters as well.

items.statement: CAPEX spend in FY25 was Rs. 5,700 million, primarily on Granules Life Sciences.
items.quote: CAPEX spend during the quarter was Rs. 1,598 million, and for the year was Rs. 5,700 million, primarily invested in Granules Life Sciences of Rs. 3,135 million in FY '25.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement due to strategic shift towards high-margin formulation products.
items.quote: The full year gross margin as a percentage of sales for FY '25 is up by 635 basis points from FY '24. Margin improvement is due to strategical shift towards high margin formulation products.

items.statement: Lisdexamfetamine API validation and DMF filing expected in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Furthermore, API validation and DMF filing is expected to be done in quarter one FY '26 for lisdexamfetamine, which leads to vertical integration and supply chain reliability for this product.

items.statement: Expects double-digit revenue growth and EBITDA margin of 12-14% for the group, excluding SCS.
items.quote: We expect that the group will have double -digit revenue growth. This is even excluded even SCS, we still expect to have double-digit EBITDA I mean, double-digit revenue growth, and we expect EBITDA margin to be 12% to 14%.

items.statement: SCS expected to reach EBITDA positive by Q4 and consolidate under SCD in FY27.
items.quote: we think the SCS as a group will certainly reach EBITDA positive by Q4, and we will then consolidate completely in FY '27 under SCD.

items.statement: Capex budget for the group is INR160 crores for the current year.
items.quote: I think the total capex budget for the current year is INR160 crores.

items.statement: Sees robust order book at SCD with traction in all locations.
items.quote: We see a robust order book at SCD. We're getting traction in all the locations.

items.statement: Most duties passed on or solutions found with OEMs; price increases passed to customers.
items.quote: So, in summary, most of the duties have been passed on or solutions have been found with our OEMs.

items.statement: Expects DCD strong growth, especially in aftermarket and braking systems.
items.quote: we expect that to continue, especially in the aftermarket. We are seeing a lot of good traction in our braking systems.

items.statement: PLD revenue expected at similar levels, focus on margin growth.
items.quote: I think we probably will expect revenue to be at similar levels, and we'll be focusing more on margin growth.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty is a major challenge, with timing effects unpredictable.
items.quote: Challenge is, of course, when somebody can tweet a change of tariff, we don't know what's happening. So that's the major most major uncertainty in this.

items.statement: SCS expected revenue around USD 40 million for the full year.
items.quote: The business of that SCS to be generally give an idea, will be around USD 40 million for the full year.

items.statement: Expects further improvement in Controls Division margin, starting from Q1 onwards.
items.quote: we have clearly said there would be a further improvement in Controls Division margin for the year. I think you will start seeing that from Q1 onwards

items.statement: One-off expenses around INR25-30 crores for last year, expected to come down in FY26.
items.quote: maybe around INR25 crores, INR30 crores would be there for the last year.

items.statement: Expects double-digit growth in DCD and SCD, single-digit in PLD, double-digit in Electronics.
items.quote: we expect both the Domestic Cable Division and Suprajit Controls Division to grow in double digits for the year. This Phoenix Lamps would be although the aim is to get back to double-digit, knowing the business, I think it will be somewhere in single digits.

items.statement: Tariff pass-through to customers agreed with major Tier 1, with some burden taken.
items.quote: that Tier 1 has committed, yes, they are going to bear the burden. And this has also back-to-back, I would say, probably an agreement with the OEM also because we also had highlighted it to the OEM.

items.statement: Global automotive business expected not to grow, but company aims double-digit growth.
items.quote: Our assessment is that the global automotive business will not grow. Of course, ex India, I mean, India will grow, I guess. But since we have 50% of our business is dependent on it, we are still saying that we will grow our business in double -digit.

items.statement: Electronics Division gaining orders in instrument clusters, sensors, and actuators.
items.quote: One is the driver information system or the instrument clusters as we call them, yes, the combi meters as the Japanese call them. That is one area that we are gaining, I would say, orders.

items.statement: No further write-offs expected for EV customers in Electronics Division.
items.quote: So whatever write -offs we had to take for certain EV customers, we have already taken. Therefore, there are no more of them coming and hitting our books.

items.statement: Targets INR12,000 crores turnover by FY31.
items.quote: Having said that, we have given a guidan ce of INR12,000 crores turnover by FY '31 and I think we are very well on line for the same

items.statement: Expects 20% growth in laminates this year.
items.quote: This year we are very confident of a 20% growth and in line with that, we have seen a good April and a good May.

items.statement: Targets 8-10% EBITDA margin for laminates by H2.
items.quote: For the curren t year, we are looking at 8% to 10% EBITDA margin towards the end of H2 and I think we will be o nline to achieve the

items.statement: New particle board plant expected to achieve 15%+ EBITDA margin at steady state.
items.quote: So on a steady state basis, this plant should definitely give us a 15% plus EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Aims to maintain 12-14% plywood EBITDA margin.
items.quote: Going forward also I will still maintain we will try to deliver a 12% to 14%.

items.statement: MDF demand expected to grow at 20% plus.
items.quote: MDF demand is likely to continue to grow at 20% plus. The market h as been growing at close to 20% and I believe that the market is likely to continue growing at 20

items.statement: Expects MDF price hikes towards end of year.
items.quote: But the expectation is towards the end of the year, there should be certain price rises in MDF.

items.statement: Took 2% price increase in Century brand plywood in April.
items.quote: But we ourselves have taken a price increase in April of 2% in our Century brand.

items.statement: No MDF price cuts taken; only periodic schemes.
items.quote: We have taken no price cuts. There are schemes that we give to th e market periodically

items.statement: Hoshiarpur plywood plant to add 48,000 CBM capacity in 15 months.
items.quote: So the capacity utilization currently is about 90% for this entire year and already we've announced the Hoshiarpur plant, which will come about in the next 15 months, which will help us with our futuristic growth and we are expecting that to be about 48,000 CBM more.

items.statement: MDF line expansion planned between September and December, shutdown 30-40 days.
items.quote: Between September and December of this year we should go for the e xpansion. However, we have not taken a concrete date yet. It will depend on how util izations take place and when we can build up sufficient inventory. It is going to be a shutdown that is in excess of 30 to 40 days

items.statement: Substantial laminate order book; Badvel plant achieved highest monthly turnover.
items.quote: Yes, we have a substantial order book. And in fact I'm very hap py to share that last month was the highest turnover that the Badvel plant has ever done for

items.statement: MDF overcapacity at 15-20% oversupply.
items.quote: So still we would be at around 15%, 20% oversupply at this point of time

items.statement: Plans to repay majority of debt over next two years, low long-term debt by FY27.
items.quote: With regards to debt, I think we are at peak debt like I had already mentioned. And over the course of the next two years, we'll be repaying the majority of debt. So I think we'll be at very, very low long-term debt by the end of FY '27.

items.statement: Expects to reduce inventory days by close to 10 days this year.
items.quote: So going forward I'm hopeful that over the course of the current year, we will reduce inventory days by close to 10 days.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth outlook of 20% to 25% for FY26 in line with 20% CAGR NorthStar target
items.quote: So we continue to maintain an outlook of, again, 20% to 25% growth on the consolidated revenues, in line with our 20.20.20.20 theme of growing at a minimum 20% CAGR.

items.statement: Greenfuel Energy Solutions revenue guidance for FY26 maintained at INR 300-350 crore
items.quote: So the guidance for FY '26 of Greenfuel would be continuing to be similar between INR 300 crore to INR 350 crore.

items.statement: IAC India growth expected at 10% to 15% CAGR on higher base going forward
items.quote: As a part of our next midterm plan, we expect IAC growth to be more in the vicinity of around 10% to 15% CAGR.

items.statement: Aftermarket division targeting upwards of 15% growth in FY26
items.quote: we should be able to again come back and deliver a very handsome growth, maybe upwards of 15% odd for aftermarket division.

items.statement: Alps Alpine JV expected to deliver INR 120 crore revenue in FY26 from INR 50 crore in FY25
items.quote: Alps Alpine registered a revenue of around INR 50 crore in FY25. It is expected to deliver INR 120 crore in FY26.

items.statement: Lumax Yokowo, Lumax Ituran, Lumax Alps subsidiaries foreseen to grow at 30%-40% CAGR over next 2-3 years
items.quote: there we foresee a significant growth, perhaps even in the next 2 to 3 years, a CAGR of upwards of 30% -40%.

items.statement: EBITDA target to double from INR 500+ crore to possibly cross INR 1,000 crore by FY28
items.quote: by FY28, we are fairly certain that with the accelerated growth on subsidiaries on the aftermarket and getting full year realizations of certain inorganic strategic Lumax Auto Technologies Limited May 30, 2025 initiatives, we should be able to double our EBITDA from the last year's upwards of INR 500 crore to possibly crossing the INR 1,000 crore mark by FY28

items.statement: Consolidated capex plan for FY26 around INR 175-200 crore similar to FY25
items.quote: The capex plan for the consolidated entity would be anywhere around a similar number as FY25, around INR 175 crore to INR 200 crore around that vicinity.

items.statement: Robust order book of INR 1,300 crore with 26% (INR 333 crore) materializing in FY26, 42% in FY27, 32% in FY28
items.quote: We are pleased to report a robust order book of INR 1,300 crore with strong visibility across next 3 fiscal years. Of this, approximately 26% is projected to materialize in FY26, 42% in FY27 and the remaining 32% in FY28.

items.statement: BEV platforms constitute ~40% (INR 500 crore) of total order book
items.quote: So from the total order book of INR 1,300 crore, the BEV is almost 40% of the total order book. So that is close to approximately INR 500-odd crore is from BEVs platforms.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to expand by 100-200 bps by FY28 driven by subsidiary growth and inorganic realizations
items.quote: if we are able to do that, I think you will start seeing EBITDA margins expand by about close to 100-200 bps.

items.statement: Long-term NorthStar target of nearing 20% EBITDA margin not time-bound to 6 years
items.quote: We have not anywhere said that we want to achieve 20% in the next 6 years. I think as a part of the investor presentation also, we say that the 20% EBITDA margin is a NorthStar where we wish to inch closer towards those margin levels. It is not time specific to 6 years.

items.statement: Advanced plastics largest share of order book, followed by mechatronics and structures & control systems
items.quote: The order book reflects healthy traction across all product verticals with advanced pl astics contributing the largest share, followed by mechatronics and structures and control systems

items.statement: Growth derisked by diversity of products, companies and OEMs; only black swan events pose risk
items.quote: I think if there is, of course, an unforeseen black swan event in the industry, then of course, it carries its own risk. But I think with the given diversity of products, companies as well as OEMs, we are fairly derisked from this kind of growth opportunity.

items.statement: By end of next year, BPM revenue mix expected ~32% digital and 68% traditional; in three years ratio expected to reverse.
items.quote: Secondly, regarding our revenue mix of the BPM business, by the end of next year, we expect it to be approximately 32% digital and 68% traditional business. However, in the next three years, this ratio is expected to reverse, with a significant increase in digital revenue streams.

items.statement: Onshore footprint to be significantly reduced; offshore presence expanding in South Africa, Jamaica, Colombia, India, Philippines.
items.quote: Currently, a significant portion of our BPM business operates onshore, but we anticipate a gradual reduction in our onshore footprint, given the lower-margin nature of these operations. Instead, we are expanding our offshore presence, with new centers established in South Africa, Jamaica, and Colombia, alongside existing hubs in India and the Philippines.

items.statement: When clients transition from onshore to offshore, billing rates typically decrease by ~50%, but margins improve.
items.quote: It is important to note that when a client transitions from onshore to offshore, billing rates typically decrease by approximately 50%, given the lower cost base in offshore locations such as India and the Philippines. While this results in a reduction in revenue, it simultaneously enhances margin performance as we optimize delivery costs.

items.statement: Cash reserves primarily for acquisitions; considering mix of smaller or larger deals, no exact timeline.
items.quote: Our cash has primarily been deployed toward acquisitions, including: • TekLink acquisition • Acquisition of our Australian business • Greenfield expansion in Colombia and South Africa going forward, our primary use of these funds remains focused on acquisitions.

items.statement: Acquisitions will be thoroughly evaluated factoring strategic capabilities, technology, client value, fair valuation.
items.quote: Any acquisitions we pursue will be thoroughly evaluated, factoring in: 1. Strategic capabilities 2. Technology and innovation 3. Potential client value 4. Fair valuation

items.statement: Considering mix of potential transactions, multiple smaller deals or few larger acquisitions; difficult to specify exact number or timeline.
items.quote: To provide directional clarity, we are considering a mix of potential transactions —this could involve multiple smaller deals or a few larger acquisitions.
