While it is difficult to specify an exact number or timeline at this stage, this represents the broad trajectory we are targeting.

items.statement: In FY2026, plan to launch initial set of prioritized solutions and establish dedicated package solutions team.
items.quote: In FY2026, we plan to launch an initial set of prioritized solutions, aligned with market demand. To support this, we will establish a dedicated package solutions team encompassing product development, delivery, R&D, and go-to-market efforts.

items.statement: Strategy for FY26 continues to align with expanding broadband in Tier-2/3 markets and CelerityX.
items.quote: Looking ahead, our strategy for FY '26 continues to align with this direction. As referenced on Slide 21, this approach will be further expanded to enhance market penetration and profitability.

items.statement: Plan to replicate mini-entrepreneur model in broadband, collaborating with local entrepreneurs; IPTV tested in Bengaluru, intend nationwide deployment.
items.quote: Building on this success, we plan to replicate the model in broadband expansion, collaborating with local entrepreneurs to develop a network of digital service providers, including broadband and IPTV offerings. o IPTV services have been successfully tested in Bengaluru , and we intend to extend deployment nationwide

items.statement: Onboarding senior leadership across commercial control, product development, customer experience to support expansion.
items.quote: To support this expansion, we are onboarding senior leadership across domains such as commercial control, product development, and customer experience.

items.statement: Working on cost savings and rationalization, began last year, expect more traction through rest of this year.
items.quote: We are obviously focused on all opportunities to grow revenue. More importantly, we are working on cost savings and rationalization. This is something we began last year and expect to see more traction on through the rest of this year.

items.statement: Looking to leverage existing DTV customer base to sell other services like broadband, rather than directly growing DTV segment.
items.quote: Coming to specifics, Vyns spoke about some of the challenges in the DTV business. We’re now looking to leverage our existing DTV customer base to sell other services like broadband, rather than directly growing the DTV segment.

items.statement: Focus on growing CX business in offshore markets where margin realization is higher; prioritize expansion in cost-efficient delivery locations.
items.quote: Our focus has been on growing the CX business in offshore markets, where revenue per client may be lower in absolute dollar terms but margin realization is significantly higher. Consequently, our strategy prioritizes expansion in cost -efficient delivery locations, such as India, the Philippines, Colombia, Jamaica, and South Africa, where we recently opened a center.

items.statement: Focus on expanding onshore operations remains limited; actively shifted service delivery from onshore to offshore where possible.
items.quote: On the onshore side, revenue margins tend to be lower, and accordingly, our focus on expanding onshore operations remains limited. Wherever possible and with client agreement, we have actively shifted service delivery from onshore locations to offshore centers.

items.statement: Strategic priority is expanding digital and technology services; continue exploring cross-selling opportunities.
items.quote: As Venk mentioned, our strategic priority is expanding digital and technology services, which aligns with long -term growth objectives. Additionally, we continue exploring cross -selling opportunities, both within our existing client base and by acquiring new customers to drive revenue expansion.

items.statement: Actively rationalizing expenses, reducing overseas real estate, centralizing operations, leveraging lower-cost locations for internal services and tech delivery.
items.quote: On the cost optimization front, we are actively rationalizing expenses wherever feasible. This includes reducing overseas real estate footprint, centralizing operations, and leveraging lower-cost locations like India and the Philippines for internal services and tech delivery.

items.statement: Expects direct-to-consumer segment to grow 40-50% in current year.
items.quote: So, I think that clearly within our three segments, we anticipate that we will grow our top line in our direct-to-consumer segment by 40% to 50% in the current year.

items.statement: Expects licensed brands to grow in low double digits.
items.quote: So, I think we expect licensed brands to grow in low double digits.

items.statement: Expects customer brand segment to be steady and probably mid-single digits.
items.quote: I think the customer brand segment would be steady and probably will be mid-single digits.

items.statement: Expects own brands to grow by 50% without growth in India retail business.
items.quote: As of right now, in the current year we anticipate that without any growth in the India retail business our own brands should grow by 50%.

items.statement: Expects lab grown to become majority of business over next 2 years.
items.quote: I think going forward we would fully expect that lab grown will become the majorit y of our business over the next 2 years.

items.statement: Anticipates further reduction in gross debt by 31st March 2026.
items.quote: Furthermore, we anticipate a further reduction in gross debt by 31st March 2026.

items.statement: Expects FY26 to begin on a soft note due to US trade tariffs.
items.quote: We expect FY26 to begin on a soft note due to the economic uncertainty created by US trade tariffs.

items.statement: Plans to open flagship Jean Dousset store in New York City in Q3.
items.quote: During this year we plan to increase the physical footprint of Jean Dousset as it's an omnichannel business that has tremendous potential going forward by opening a flagship location in New York City in Q3 of the current financial year.

items.statement: Cost optimization program projected to deliver annual savings of Rs. 40-50 crores.
items.quote: This initiative is projected to deliver annual savings of Rs. 40 crores to Rs. 50 crores.

items.statement: Bhavnagar facility closure to result in annual savings of 20 crores.
items.quote: The closure of the Bhavnagar facility will result in annual savings of 20 crores in itself.

items.statement: Estimates cost savings of 50 to 60 crores from restructuring.
items.quote: I would say that 50 to 60 crores is a good estimate of cost savings that we would incur.

items.statement: Working with customers to pass on tariffs; most have agreed, but 45-60 day impact on P&L.
items.quote: We are working with all of our customers to pass on the tariffs to them. Since a lot of our customers are domestic customers , contractually there was a period of time where we were unable to pass on the increased tariffs for a 2-month period.

items.statement: Approximate impact on bottom line from tariffs roughly Rs. 10 crores for the quarter.
items.quote: I would say that the approximate impact would be roughly Rs. 10 crores for the quarter.

items.statement: No degrowth in revenue due to tariffs; US consumer resilient, no impact on demand.
items.quote: We are not going to have a degrowth in revenue due to the tariff issues because we took a call as a company to ship all orders that we had to our customers because a lot of our contracts with our customers are domestic where we clear the product in the US .

items.statement: Backup plan to manufacture in UAE if reciprocal tariffs on India come into effect.
items.quote: So, there are obviously rules around country of origin. And we do have a backup plan in terms of manufacturing goods in the UAE.

items.statement: Raised Rs. 163 crores through preferential issue during the year.
items.quote: We also bolstered our overall liq uidity by raising Rs. 163 crores through a preferential issue during the year.

items.statement: Expects 8-10% volume growth in coming days.
items.quote: And I believe we should be able to deliver 8 % to 10% volume growth in coming days.

items.statement: Aims for 14-15% EBITDA margin, sustainable and achievable.
items.quote: I'm still having a belief that 14%-15% margins are really sustainable achievable margin, and we aspire to reach to that level.

items.statement: Margin improvement expected from July quarter, reaching expectations by Q3.
items.quote: I would say you will see from July quarter, which is the second quarter you will see upside from July onwards and by third quarter you will see that the results are coming to our expectation.

items.statement: Earmarked Rs. 150 crores CAPEX for coming year.
items.quote: We have also earmarked Rs. 150 crores in CAPEX for the coming year to build and execute our strategic pillars as highlighted by Parmodji.

items.statement: Price increase of Rs. 11-12 crores effective July/August.
items.quote: I got a price increase of almost Rs. 11-12 crores. But the effective date is 1st of July, 1 st of August because the long -term contract is in place.

items.statement: Alumina prices declined from Rs. 95,000 to Rs. 77,000 per ton, expected to fall further.
items.quote: Fortunately now, alumina prices are going down. From 95 000, it has reached to Rs. 77,000. It will go down further.

items.statement: Reduced price inventory to benefit from July onward, improving margins next quarter.
items.quote: I believe July onward, we should be having this reduced price inventory in our system and next quarter should see improvement in margin for sure.

items.statement: Domestic steel demand expected to rise in FY26.
items.quote: India's steel sector remains a cornerstone of economic growth, with domestic demand expected to rise in FY'26, fueled by infrastructure investment, the national logistic policy, and Make in India initiative with export of 12% import duty restrictions.

items.statement: Cement demand projected to grow 6-8% in FY26.
items.quote: The demand projected to grow 6 % to 8% in FY '26, backed by an increase in government CAPEX of about 10%, driven by affordable housing, urban development, and higher projects.

items.statement: Specialty products constitute 25-30% of total steel segment.
items.quote: Normally, specialty products are to the tune of 25% to 30% of total steel.

items.statement: Overcapacity from competitors adding 150,000-170,000 tons in next year.
items.quote: Basically on paper, the projects announced by our competition or refractory industry is about 150,000 tons to 170,000 tons, which will come up in next one year or so.

items.statement: Chinese imports and overcapacity causing price erosion.
items.quote: However, the announced over capacity expansion in India coupled with Chinese import of refract ory materials is becoming a systematic iss ue resulting in price erosions.

items.statement: Export revenue target to increase to 30% of total.
items.quote: Historically before we acquired Dalmia etc., our export revenue was about 22%-23%. It is still at that level, and I keep on saying our ambition is to take it to 30% in that in RHI Magnesita India Limited because from Dalmia plants we are not doing any export at all.

items.statement: New magnesium carbon bricks production to add Rs. 100 crores next year.
items.quote: And then we have a strong market also for magnesium carbon and our Cuttack plant is full running at full capacity and now from last month we start producing in Rajgangpur Dalmia plant about 600-700 ton of this magnesium carbon bricks also for steel industry which we will ramp up to 1000 ton every month. So that will also give us about Rs. 100 crore or so next year.

items.statement: Local for local production to add Rs. 100 crores next year.
items.quote: And from Jan onward, if trials went well, probably it will add Rs. 100 crores for next year in that particular segment only.

items.statement: Targeting over 50% AUM growth for the current year.
items.quote: And as you asked about the AUM target, with lenders, we are at least targeting a 50% growth. In fact, over 50% growth in AUM for the current year.

items.statement: Opex target between 11% and 12%.
items.quote: Opex, I believe it should be between 11 % and 12%. It all depends on how soon we are able to grow our AUM. Our target would be to remain anywhere between 11% to 12%.

items.statement: Credit cost expected around 3% for the current year.
items.quote: So my guess is that, but given that there is some portfolio which has already moved to NPA, maybe around, you know, 3% kind of credit cost we still see for the current year.

items.statement: Targeting approximately 65% secured AUM by March 26.
items.quote: This steady progres s puts us firmly on track to reach a target of approximately 65% secured AUM by March 26, reflecting our strategic shift towards building a more resilient and lower risk portfolio.

items.statement: Secured share to reach 75% plus in FY27, likely 80%.
items.quote: And in 27, it will be 75% plus. So it could be around 75% to 80%, more likely 80 than 75.

items.statement: Opex to reduce below 10% over next two years.
items.quote: We are targeting to bring down our opex below 10% over the next two years, supported by growth in AUM and ongoing efficiency improvements.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing to decline by at least 3% to 3.5% over next two to three years.
items.quote: Right now, our average COB is 13%, although incremental is at around 12 now. So there is a scope of about minimum 3% to 3.5% reduction over the next two, three years.

items.statement: FY26 to be year of recovery, FY27 significantly better.
items.quote: It will be , '26 will be the year of recovery, where I see that on the financials, as I already said that 1 year got lost. But this year will be the year of recovery. And '27 would look very, very significantly better.

items.statement: Net worth to improve with INR85 crores pending from share warrants.
items.quote: Net worth will significantly improve this year as well as INR85 crores in pending from the issue of share warrants.

items.statement: Branch network to expand to 175 plus by March 2026.
items.quote: We plan to expand this further to 175 plus branches by March 2026, ensuring deeper penetration and better service delivery across regions.

items.statement: Visibility of INR500 crores per annum through lending collaborations.
items.quote: On the partnership front, we now have visibility of INR500 crores per annum through lending collaboration, including business correspondence and co-lending model arrangements.

items.statement: Rural demand reasonable and improving month on month.
items.quote: I think it is reasonable. I will not say that it is sharply up, but it is reasonable. The month on month situation is improving.

items.statement: Cattle portfolio proportion to reduce to 50% over a few years.
items.quote: So maybe in a few years, it will come down to 50% of our portfolio.

items.statement: No further stress expected beyond what has already occurred.
items.quote: But I think from here on, we don't see any further, you know, anything worse happening. I mean, it's on the positive side only.

items.statement: Collection efficiency stabilization expected in Q1.
items.quote: In terms of 0 to 90 bucket, I believe that the stabilization is seen in Q1.

items.statement: Expects consolidated revenue between INR 1,600 crores and INR 1,800 crores for FY26.
items.quote: Yes, between INR 1,600 crores to INR 1,800 crores, including the standalone companies, S.P. Apparels' additional capacity of Sivakasi and other things, and put all together, I think we expect as a consolidated number of between INR 1,600 crores to INR 1,800 crores.

items.statement: Aims for top line of INR 2,000 crores by FY27.
items.quote: By end of FY26, e anticipate to operate approximately 7,500 machines, which includes Young Brand Apparel also. With this, we aim to achieve a top line of INR 2,000 crores by FY27.

items.statement: Guides standalone EBITDA margin of 18%.
items.quote: On standalone basis, we are guiding for an 18% EBITDA.

items.statement: Expects Young Brand EBITDA margin to improve from 15% to 16% or 17%.
items.quote: And Young Brand, we expect to improve from 15% to maybe 16% or 17%, which we are yet to see.

items.statement: Plans consolidated capex of INR 60 crores plus $6 million for FY26.
items.quote: Consol capex should be around INR 60 crores in terms of capex. For Sti Lanka, the $6 million unsecured loan transferred to the subsidiary company.

items.statement: Current order book is INR 442 crores.
items.quote: The current order book status is INR442 crores.

items.statement: SPUK current order book is GBP 4.4 million.
items.quote: Yes, GBP 4.4 million already. So, we will be able to close between GBP 9 million to GBP 10 million for FY26.

items.statement: Expects SPUK revenue of GBP 12 million to GBP 14 million in FY27.
items.quote: So, FY27 should be at least about GBP 12 million to GBP 14 million.

items.statement: Expects INR 200 crores revenue from Sri Lanka in FY26.
items.quote: Sri Lanka, we are expecting 1,000 machines. So, it is about INR 200 crores in FY25-26.

items.statement: Expects INR 35 crores to INR 40 crores revenue from Sivakasi for full year.
items.quote: We can expect INR 35 crores to INR 40 crores from Sivakasi.

items.statement: Expects Young Brand revenue closer to INR 350 crores next year.

items.statement: Working capital cycle target 50-55 days, cash flow positive by FY27.

items.statement: Expects 70:30 domestic to export ratio, with India 70-75% and exports 20-30%.
items.quote: So, it will not be like we are going for 60%, 70% export. But again, there can be a 70:30 ratio. So going ahead, India can be 70%-75%, and export can be 20%-25% or 30%.

items.statement: FY26 exit run rate of 650-700 kg per month.
items.quote: Yes, 650 to 700 kgs per month, yes.

items.statement: Gold price volatility causing inventory shifts and ticket size reduction.

items.statement: New ERP system to be operational this year.

items.quote: For FY '26, I think we are actually looking at 100 basis points down.

items.statement: FY26 net new money target for Nuvama Private ARR assets is INR10,000-11,000 crores (25-30% on opening book)
items.quote: If we are able to do anywhere between 25-30% on that, so you are again looking at INR10,000 crores to INR11,000 crores coming from there is what we will target.

items.statement: FY26 net new money target for Nuvama Wealth MPIS assets is INR7,000-8,000 crores (25-30% on opening book)
items.quote: Similarly, on the Wealth side, now our MPIS book would be around maybe INR30,000 crores, again, a 25-30%, so maybe INR7,000 - 8,000 crores there.

items.statement: FY26 Asset Management net new money target is INR5,000-6,000 crores (CRE INR2,000-2,300 cr, public markets INR3,000-4,000 cr, private markets INR800-1,000 cr)
items.quote: So, if you add all this together, we are again order of magnitude INR5,000 - 6,000 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated FY26 net new money target (excl. credit fund) is INR23,000-24,000 crores at bare minimum
items.quote: So, if I add all this together, we come back to some INR23,000 - 24,000 crores at the bare minimum is what we target.

items.statement: Asset Management business expected to breakeven on quarterly basis around mid-FY27 at ~INR20,000 crores AUM
items.quote: I think FY '27 somewhere around the middle is when we should start seeing that business breakeven on a quarterly basis.

items.statement: Opex growth expected to remain close to 10% year-on-year in FY26 similar to FY25
items.quote: I think we will be in the similar ZIP code in terms of opex growth year-on-year. So close to 10% seems reasonable, and that's our expectation.

items.statement: Investment Banking has 30-35 signed IPO mandates and 10-15 advisory mandates (mostly sell-side) in pipeline
items.quote: IPO, in my view, we have 30 to 35 mandates which are signed. Now we will wait for the market condition, investor appetite and all that. So, you are going to see that coming through.

items.statement: Nuvama Wealth lending steady-state NIM 5-5.5%; Nuvama Private lending steady-state NIM 4.5-5%
items.quote: I think the steady state for our Wealth business would be anywhere between 5-5.5% and for our Private business would be again between 4.5-5%.

items.statement: Asset Services clearing yield new normal expected at 1.8-1.9% (vs 1.61% FY25) assuming some FD yield decline in H2
items.quote: So actually, clearing business, I think the new normal should be closer to maybe 1.8-1.9%.

items.statement: Commercial Real Estate Fund first close done at INR1,700 crores; targeting INR4,000 crores in next 2-3 quarters; first deployment INR460 cr equity value Delhi office asset >95% leased
items.quote: The next phase will be to take this fund from current INR1,700 crores to INR4,000 crores in maybe next two to three quarters.

items.statement: Private Credit fund team being finalized; target launch by Q3 or Q4 FY26
items.quote: We are in the process of identifying and closing the team, and maybe by Q3 or Q4, we should be up and running with that.

items.statement: Management sees 'madness' in market hiring and compensation; warns many firms will get decimated when cycle turns
items.quote: I think in a sense, there's some sort of madness happening in the market right now, the way people are building out teams and the way compensation has been dea lt, I don't know, it looks like a race to death

items.statement: Nuvama Private corporate treasury book not more than INR10,000 crores out of INR1.99 lakh crores total assets
items.quote: Total Nuvama Private, the asset size is about INR1.99 lakh crores. In that, the corporate treasury book should not be more than INR10,000 crores.

items.statement: No PAG exit development to report; management only aware of same public news articles
items.quote: I have also read the same news article, Sanketh. If there is anything which has to be reported, we will report to the exchange. There is no such development which has happened.

items.statement: Targeting more than 30% revenue growth in FY26
items.quote: Our FY ‘25 revenue growth was 30%, and we expect to deliver similar or better growth rates in FY ‘26 also.

items.statement: Targeting EBITDA margin above 4% for full year FY26
items.quote: We are targeting to exceed 4% EBITDA margins in FY ‘26 on a full year basis.

items.statement: Targeting operating cash flow positive for full year FY26
items.quote: Fourth, our focus would be on improving working capital management, which in combination with margin expansion would provide positive approaching cash flows in full year ‘26.

items.statement: Organic growth expected at 1.5x to 2x IPM growth rate
items.quote: Our organic growth has consistently tracked 1.5 to 2 times of IPM growth rate, and we expect this to continue.

items.statement: Assuming 8% IPM growth and 15-16% organic growth for FY26 guidance
items.quote: 8% IPM growth, 15% to 16% organic growth.

items.statement: Targeting 5% improvement in net working capital days for FY26
items.quote: There's definitely 5% improvement that we are planning for next year.

items.statement: Targeting 60 days working capital cycle in near term (2-3 years)
items.quote: I think long term is very long, but in near term it is 60 days. Yes. I mean, next two -three, two years we should target that 60 days.

items.statement: Corporate tax rate guidance of 25% for FY26
items.quote: See, corporate tax rate is 25%. So corporates make an effort to optimize on tax rate through more tax efficient strategies. But for the time being , you can take the guidance of 25% corporate tax rate.

items.statement: No immediate fund raise planned; unutilized IPO proceeds and balance sheet cash sufficient for acquisitions
items.quote: See as of now we do not have a new fundraise plan , okay. Because the IPO that we did a year back has given us, we still have unutilized proceeds from that IPO and on our balance sheet also we have significant cash.

items.statement: Six new strategic acquisitions announced adding over Rs. 400 crores annualized revenue
items.quote: We have already announced six new strategic acquisitions which collectively would add over Rs. 400 crores of annualized revenues and expand our geographical reach and further add to our business portfolio in the areas of trade generics, specialty pharma, medical consumables and devices.

items.statement: Acquired businesses are EBITDA margin accretive at 6-8% range
items.quote: In one of the previous presentations you have mentioned that the acquisitions’ EBITDA margin range is roughly about 6% to 8%. Would these acquisitions also being in that range, can I assume that? Prabhat Agarwal: Yes.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin target moving towards 5%
items.quote: So, for example, I have said that next year is 4% plus, and earlier I had told about we should be targeting close to 5%, right? So the year beyond we should reach towards that or move towards that.

items.statement: Industry growth slowed to 8% in FY25 with last two quarters at 7%
items.quote: If you look at the last year, the entire year the industry growth rate was only 8% and the last two quarters were like 7% right. So, historically industry has grown in double digits earlier and which has come down to single digits for the last year, right.

items.statement: OTC policy shift to kirana stores could reduce addressable market if not adapted
items.quote: If part of the sales of OTC moves away from retail pharmacy to kirana stores, either we will have to prepare a plan to reach out to kirana stores or the industry size will become smaller for us. Our addressable market will become a little smaller for us.

items.statement: Full year impact of FY25 acquisitions estimated at Rs. 1,000 crores with Rs. 500 crores delta for FY26
items.quote: Delta would be around Rs. 500 crores.

items.statement: Acquisition multiples guided at 5x-7x EV/EBITDA
items.quote: The guidance that we give is the multiples are between 5 x to 7x times of EV to EBITDA, so within that range.

items.statement: Grand Showroom expected to contribute Rs. 27-28 crores in current year.
items.quote: And we anticipate in the current year, Grand Showroom itself to contribute roughly around Rs. 27 crores to Rs. 28 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expansion expected in FY26 due to healthy top line and flow-through improvement.
items.quote: You know, the flow -through will improve further, and we will see scope for margin expansion in FY ‘26.

items.statement: Bengaluru asset completion capex expected Rs. 70-100 crores.
items.value: Rs. 70 crores to Rs. 100 odd crores
items.quote: As we said, the asset we would spend roughly around Rs. 70 crores to Rs. 100 odd crores is a broad range for CAPEX for Bengaluru completion.

items.statement: Kaziranga asset built at Rs. 1.2-1.5 crore per key.
items.value: Rs. 1.2 crores to Rs. 1.5 crore a key
items.quote: So the Kaziranga asset will be built at about Rs. 1.2 crores to Rs. 1.5 crore a key.

items.statement: Additional 250 keys in Bangalore to cost approximately Rs. 2 crore per key, totaling about Rs. 500 crore.
items.value: Rs. 2 crore per key, about Rs. 500 crore
items.quote: So, Bangalore asset, the additional that we had said, the 250 that will be built, that would cost approximately Rs. 2 crore. So, that's about Rs. 500 crore.

items.statement: Guwahati asset to be built at Rs. 1.2-1.5 crore per key.
items.value: Rs. 1.2 crores to Rs. 1.5 crore per key
items.quote: And the Guwahati asset again would be about Rs. 1.2 crores to Rs. 1.5 crore per key.

items.statement: Additional 500 keys under discussion at Rs. 1.2-1.5 crore per key.
items.value: Rs. 1.2 crores to Rs. 1.5 crores a key
items.quote: And the additional 500 that we said that it is under discussion, again the approximate value per key would be about Rs. 1.2 crores to Rs. 1.5 crores a key.

items.statement: Planning to add 2,072 keys to existing 1,895 keys over next three years.
items.quote: With the above initiatives, we are actively working on adding 2,072 keys to our existing portfolio of 1,895 keys over the next three years.

items.statement: Bangalore hotel expected to complete by end of FY26.
items.quote: The hotel is expected to complete by financial year, end of the Financial Year '26, that is, in next nine months.

items.statement: Kaziranga project slated for completion by FY28.
items.quote: The project is slated for completion by Financial Year '28.

items.statement: Hyatt Regency Mumbai expected operational in last quarter of current financial year.
items.quote: So, I would expect it to be in the last quarter of this current financial year.

items.statement: Huge demand rise for slow months, potential growth of almost 12% across hotels.
items.quote: But this year we see a huge, huge demand rise compared to last year for these slow months, and our books overall on all our hotels have shown a potential growth of almost 12%.

items.statement: Grand Hyatt ARR headroom of Rs. 2,000-3,000 given market conditions.
items.quote: I believe there is still a headroom of another Rs. 2,000 to Rs. 3,000 given market conditions.

items.statement: Kaziranga ARRs expected Rs. 12,000-15,000.
items.quote: It would range from Rs. 12,000 to Rs. 15,000 starting..

items.statement: May saw some impact from cross-border escalations, but business strong and recovery expected by year-end.
items.quote: May, of course, as everyone else has iterated, there is some impact, but we believe the business is strong.

items.statement: ROFO assets intended to be acquired via cashless share swap.
items.quote: I would also like to clarify something which we have shared in the past, is that the ROFO asset, the intent is to do it in a cashless share swap manner.

items.statement: Long-term 15% growth guidance remains unchanged.
items.quote: we have given a guidance of 15% growth year-on-year. That on a long-term basis continues to be the same.

items.statement: Aim to return to FY24 EBITDA margin of 5.1% in FY26.
items.quote: We would want to get back to the EBITDA margins of 5.1% which we have clocked in FY ‘24. That is our aim irrespective of the cost of JLR, Nagpur new setup that is coming up or any other, the Karnataka setup which we have started in Arena.

items.statement: Plans capex of Rs. 30 crores for next financial year, excluding acquisitions.
items.quote: CAPEX we are planning is about Rs. 30 crores for the next financial year. This excludes any acquisition that we are already in discussions with.

items.statement: Board approved divestment of two subsidiaries for Rs. 70 crores, expected completion by July.
items.quote: I am pleased to share that the Board of Directors has approved the divestment of both these entities for total consideration of Rs. 70 crores. We anticipate the transaction will be completed by July.

items.statement: Sales manpower productivity initiative to add ~3,000 cars and Rs. 4-5 crores annual gain.
items.value: 3,000 cars; Rs. 4 crores to Rs. 5 crores
items.quote: This initiative is expected to result in an incremental volume of this year of about 3,000 cars and going forward at a much larger number per se and also anticipate an increase in the finance income per car, translating to an annual gain of approximately Rs. 4 crores to Rs. 5 crores.

items.statement: Service revenue per car rising by ~Rs. 300, adding ~Rs. 4 crores this year.
items.quote: On the service front, average revenue per car is rising by around Rs. 300, which is expected to add approximately Rs. 4 crores this year.

items.statement: One-time manpower correction to yield annualized benefit of ~Rs. 7 crores in FY26.
items.quote: We have also taken a one-time manpower correction measure, which is expected to deliver an annualized benefit of around Rs. 7 crores in FY ‘26.

items.statement: Same store volume growth expected at 4-5%.
items.quote: Same store growth, we are looking at a very muted thing. We are looking at about in terms of volume wise about 4% to 5%.

items.statement: New Bangalore outlet expected to add ~1,200 vehicles in FY26.
items.quote: from Q2 onwards, we are hoping that we will be looking at about 125 to 140 vehicles on an average, which will translate to about 1,200 vehicles for the year which is the number that we would have from the Karnataka operations.

items.statement: Discounts per car in April and May halved versus previous full year average.
items.quote: But overall, the discount per car in April and May is almost half of what it was in the previous full year average.

items.statement: Service revenue growth guidance of 20-25% over next couple of years.
items.quote: We were at 14%, but as we have given a guidance earlier also, we would like to clock our service revenue growth in the region of about 20%-25%. And going forward, we will achieve that in terms of the next couple of years.

items.statement: Inventory target: ARENA ~35 days, NEXA 41-42 days by June.
items.quote: So, ARENA we are looking at closer to about 35 days through the year in terms of inventory. And NEXA, say, by June, we should be bringing it down to about 41-42 days, and a lower number over the next three quarters.

items.statement: Debt-equity target of 1:1, with ~Rs. 200 crores leverage headroom.
items.quote: Internally we have a target that normally would like to keep our debt equity as 1 as to 1. As we speak in March, we ended up with, I think, 0.67 debt. So, we have enough leverage of around Rs. 200 crores, if at all, to make it to 1 as to 1.

items.statement: Ather EV EBITDA margin expected to exceed 5% in near future.
items.quote: Just to answer, I understood your question that 4.5% will definitely go beyond 5% is what we expect in the near future.

items.statement: JLR EBITDA margin: sales ~6%, service ~18%, total 7-9%.
items.quote: JLR in terms of sales division is about 6% and in terms of service would be about 18% in terms of EBITDA margin. John Verghese: Totally about 7% to 8%, 9% is what we are getting

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of INR 1,300 crores with EBITDA margin of 19-20%, subject to biomass tariff impact
items.quote: As mentioned during our last earnings call, we are on track to achieve a top line revenue of around INR1,300 crores in FY '26, reflecting over 50% growth compared to the FY '25 base. While we are confident of delivering an EBITDA margin in the range of 19% to 20%, the recent downward revision in tariff for our biomass power plant may impact profitability an d margins at the same is not reversed or

items.statement: INR 100 crores capex in FY26 for Anjar expansion and seamless pipe plant; maintenance capex INR 10-15 crores annually
items.quote: So as far as the new capex is concerned, we are already undergoing expansion of our new Anjar facility, of which we shall be doing another INR 100 crores of capex in FY '25, '26. And as far as our maintenance capex is concerned, that shall be always in the range of INR 10 crores to INR15 crores on overall group level.

items.statement: Order book of INR 1,275 crores as of April 30, 2025; piping segment order book INR 1,000-1,100 crores for FY26
items.quote: As of April 30, 2025, our order book stood at INR 1,275 crores, offering strong visibility going forward.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 operating EBITDA margin 22.2%, up 797 bps YoY; FY25 margin 15%, up 196 bps YoY
items.quote: Correspondingly, our operating EBITDA margin expanded by 797 basis points year-on-year and 1,868 basis points quarter -on-quarter to 22.2%. For the full year, operating EBITDA stood at INR123 crores, up 20.7% year-on-year with a margin expansion of 196 basis points to 15%.

items.statement: Oil & gas 73% of order book, power 20%; FY26 piping revenue INR 1,000-1,100 crores from India plus Thailand subsidiary
items.quote: And coming to the breakup of the oil and gas and power, we still have good orders from oil and gas. It's around 73% of the total value, what we have as of today. And from power, we have around 20%.

items.statement: Anjar facility adding 15,000 MTPA capacity by October 2025; seamless pipe plant commercial production by January 2026
items.quote: We expect to commission an additional 15,000 metric ton per annum capacity by October 2025, bringing the total capacity at Anjar, excluding heavy fabrication to 30,000 metric tons per annum. Simultaneously, the development of our high-wall seamless pipe plant is advancing on schedule. We remain on track to commence commercial production by January 2026.

items.statement: PSERC reduced biomass tariffs: Muktsar from INR 8.59 to 3.50/unit, Abohar from 7.47 to 5.42/unit; annual revenue impact INR 260M + 125M; review petition filed
items.quote: The tariff for the Muktsar plant was reduced from INR 8.59 per unit to INR 3.50 per unit, while the tariff for the Abohar plant was revised from INR7.47 per unit to INR5.42 per unit. Going forward, the annual revenue impact due to revised tariffs related to expected to be approximately INR260 million for the Muktsar plant and INR 125 million for Abohar.

items.statement: Strong pipeline from power sector (BHEL planning 10 boilers/year, 5 outsourced); ExxonMobil rate contract for 18 months expecting INR 40-50 crores in FY26
items.quote: So we got the rate contract from ExxonMobil USA. So that will be like for their various projects which they are executing it. So this recent one is for like 18 months, they have signed the rate contract, and we are expecting around INR 40 crores, INR 50 crores business in this financial year from them.

items.statement: Dow Chemical order ~$50M (75-80% execution in FY26); Linde kits orders; BHEL fittings orders INR 60-70 crores
items.quote: Sir, we have this Dow chemical order, which will be executed in this year. Apart of the Dow, we have a lot of order from this Linde now, Linde for the kits. Then fittings BHEL orders are there for the pipe fittings as on date. So these orders will be executed.

items.statement: Order booking target INR 1,600-1,700 crores in FY26; minimum order book INR 1,000 crores at any time
items.quote: The worst scenario, what I consider the hit rate will be around like INR 1,600 crores to INR 1,700 crores, w e should be booking the orders

items.statement: Logistics cost savings from Anjar facility (50% raw material imported, 50% revenue exported) to drive margin improvement
items.quote: Yes, definitely. And going forward, since 50% of our raw material we used to import and 50% of our overall revenue, we are exporting. Therefore, since the volumes of oil and gas sector jobs are quite higher, therefore, the logistics cost in -- particularly in oil and gas sector is a major cost factor, which decides the EBITDA margin. So we are going to save a lot of expenses on account of logistic

items.statement: Power sector execution cycle <1 year (9-11 months); oil & gas 6-18 months; FY26 revenue skewed to oil & gas, later years may level to 50-60% power
items.quote: Sir, in power sector, we shall not be getting more than 9 months' time. Maybe maximum 10, 11 months, but less than a year in any case.

items.statement: No US tariff impact currently; cost competitiveness protects against potential future tariffs
items.quote: No, there's absolutely no impact, sir, as of now. And even if it tomorrow comes, since our costing is much more competitive and it's going to be with all the countries. So I don't think we should have any impact on that.

items.statement: Q1 historically weak due to holidays; expect substantially better Q1 FY26 than previous years
items.quote: Sir, historically, April is the slowest month because people go on holidays and all those things. But in general also, we have a very poor quarter 1, but then subsequent quarters keep on ramping up and the quarter 4 is always the best. And the same thing is going to happen in this year also. But we shall be doing substantially much better Q1 than any other previous year, I can only tell you that.

items.statement: CWIP of INR 150 crores to be capitalized in FY26 plus INR 100 crores new capex; gross block to increase from ~INR 650 crores
items.quote: So just for clarity, sir, the CWIP as of now stands at almost INR 150 crores. That will get capitalized next year fully plus INR200 crores. So INR250 crores will get added to roughly INR650-odd crores of gross book? Sameer Agarwal : Yes. You are correct

items.statement: Q4 margins could be a good starting point for future margins, with anti-dumping adding upside.
items.quote: What I can tell you is that our margins in Q4 were significantly better than what they were for the whole year. So, if you look at that as a guidance, I think that could be a good number to begin with.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty recommended: $307 on China, $257 on Japan; expected to increase realizations.
items.quote: What DGTR has recommended to the Finance Ministry is $307 of anti-dumping duty on imports from China and $257 of anti-dumping duty for imports from Japan.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty expected to be notified in June for five years, positive for sales price and domestic quantities.
items.quote: See, according to the timeline, it should be notified within the month of June. We are very hopeful that it will be notified. And once notified, it will be for five years. It will definitely have a positive impact in terms of sales price as well as to some extent domestic quantities as well.

items.statement: Current prices are low and expected to increase.
items.quote: However, the current prices are quite low and we expect them to increase going ahead.

items.statement: Sulphur prices expected to remain high at $200+ for the year.
items.quote: And the guidance that we have got from sulphur manufacturers is that this year the sulphur prices are expected to remain on a higher level. On a $200 plus level for the year.

items.statement: Global market expected to grow 2-3% in near term.
items.quote: The global market is expected to grow at about 2%-3% over the near term.

items.statement: India demand expected at about 23,000 tons this year.
items.quote: More about 23,000 tons is what we expect to be the demand this year.

items.statement: Long-term demand growth for tires and insoluble sulphur at 2-3%.
items.quote: Anyway, in long term basis, we are only looking at 2%-3% growth in demand of tires and therefore of insoluble sulphur.

items.statement: Freight costs moderated to 7% in Q4 from 9% for the year, improving margins.
items.quote: Now, they have moderated and in the last quarter they came down from 9% for the year to 7.2% for the quarter ended March ‘25.

items.statement: If freight costs fall further, EBITDA margins will increase.
items.quote: If it comes down further obviously, it will add to the EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Only normal maintenance capex planned for FY26, typically INR10-13 crores.
items.quote: Only the normal capex that we do. I mean there is no special capex that is planned except for the normal capex.

items.statement: Focus on product innovation with customized grades for global tire manufacturers.
items.quote: Going forward, we will continue to focus on product innovation by offering customized grades that meet stringent technical specifications of global tire manufacturers

items.statement: Exports impacted by elevated freight costs due to geopolitical uncertainties.
items.quote: Exports have also been impacted by elevated freight costs driven by ongoing geopolitical uncertainties and disruptions in key shipping routes.

items.statement: Competitive intensity from Chinese suppliers continues to exert pricing pressure.
items.quote: Competitive intensity, especially from Chinese suppliers, continues to exert pricing pressure.

items.statement: Market share in domestic market is 55-58%; no significant reduction expected even without duty.
items.quote: Currently, our market share is already down to around 55%-58% in the domestic market. I do not see any significant reduction in domestic market share even if the duty is not imposed.

items.statement: Capacity utilization this year was around 70%.
items.quote: So, the capacity utilization this year has been around 70%.

items.statement: Revenue target for FY26 is between INR 700 crores and INR 850 crores
items.quote: The band is between INR 700 and INR 850 crores is our target band on the revenue.

items.statement: Peak consolidated revenue capacity post expansion is around INR 2,000 crores
items.quote: I agree, sir. That would be our peak capacity at what we are right now.

items.statement: Consolidated order backlog stands at almost INR 750 crores
items.quote: Our strong consolidated order backlog at this quarter stands almost close to INR 750 crores.

items.statement: Bid pipeline for Quality Power exceeds INR 1,000 crores and for Mehru exceeds INR 400 crores
items.quote: The bid pipeline for Quality Power as on last month is excess of INR 1,000 crores. And for Mehru is excess of INR 400 crores.

items.statement: Sangli facility capacity to increase nearly 9-fold within 18 months; Mehru capex to deliver 45% additional capacity in 4-5 months
items.quote: Overall, our production capacity in Sangli will increase nearly 9-fold within the next 18 months, with robust order booking anticipated to commence within 6-9 months.

items.statement: Blended margins expected to be around 17-18%, targeting 20%
items.quote: We believe the blended would still be upwards of 16%, 17%. We would ideally like to target 20%.

items.statement: Forecasting sustainable margins around 15-16% for FY26 and ahead
items.quote: I believe so. That is what we are forecasting.

items.statement: Demand-supply shortage in high voltage equipment (220kV+) expected to persist for 6-7 years in Europe
items.quote: Most of the European factories, on an average, are closed for 6 to 7 years. And Europe is normally the hub for all high voltage electrical equipments.

items.statement: Power quality solutions currently 40-45% of revenue; aim to reduce to 20-25% as manufacturing grows
items.quote: Our power quality is at this moment about 40%-45% of our total revenue.

items.statement: Turkey exposure minimal: <INR 8 crores spending offers from Turkish sub to India, <INR 5 crores from India to Turkey
items.quote: We have less than INR 8 crores of spending offers from our Turkish subsidiary to Indian customers, and less than INR 5 crores from Indian companies to our Turkish customers.

items.statement: Promoters extended INR 125 crore soft credit line at concessional rate
items.quote: The promoters have extended an INR 125 crore soft credit line at a concessional rate.

items.statement: Promoters waived dividends of ~INR 5 crores to conserve capital for investment cycle
items.quote: We have consciously and transparently decided to waive off our dividends, amounting to approximately INR 5 crores to conserve vital capital during this crucial investment cycle.

items.statement: Mehru order book surged beyond INR 350 crores in last few months
items.quote: The order book at Mehru has surged beyond INR 350 crores in the last few months.

items.statement: Internal budget for next year revenue north of INR 700 crores
items.quote: We believe next year our internal budgets are north of INR 700 crores.

items.statement: HVDC/FACTS factory at Sangli to be online by second half of next year; Cochin expansion for medium voltage this year
items.quote: For the HVDC and FACTS, we will be taking orders from about 6 months' time because the factory will be online by second half of next year.

items.statement: STATCOM Energy acquisition mutually called off due to misfit with investment philosophy
items.quote: So we have decided to mutually call it off.

items.statement: Targeting US$108 billion top line by 2030, ROCE 40%.
items.quote: Okay. The number of all the groups and everything put together, we are targeting for 2030 will be US$108 billion on the top line. And of course, the ROCE remains same at 40%.

items.statement: Capex guidance for next year about INR 6,000 crores plus or minus 10%.
items.quote: Looking at all these new developments, our capex guidance for the next year and including for our existing business is about INR 6,000 crores plus or minus 10%. 50% of this is regular capex and 50% is purely growth-oriented.

items.statement: Large book business order of approximately US$88 billion.
items.quote: Finally, there is no better proof of the stability and strength of the diversified business model than a large book business order of approximately US$88 billion.

items.statement: Expect stark improvement in margins next year.
items.quote: So definitely for the next year, I think you should see a stark improvement from where we are.

items.statement: In discussions with customers for pass-through of tariff-related charges, no material financial impact.
items.quote: For the remaining portion of the sales, we are in constructive discussions with our customers regarding the pass-through of tariff-related charges and do not seeing material financial impact.

items.statement: Signs of softening production volumes due to trade uncertainties and platform mix.
items.quote: As we ride through the current financial year, there are signs of softening of production volumes, driven mainly by uncertainties created by evolving trade dynamics and evolving platform mix.

items.statement: Consumer electronics on track to reach capacity of 15 to 17 million units by end of FY26.
items.quote: Consumer electronics is having a very rapid ramp-up and is on track to reach a capacity of 15 to 17 million units by the end of FY '26.

items.statement: Working capital expanded by approximately INR 2,000 crores, opportunity to reduce.
