items.quote: I think it is somewhere around 10% to 11%. I don't have the current share because the data is still not ready, but we are performing on the better than what we have written in our red book.

items.statement: Six direct and four contract food processing facilities.
items.quote: For food processing, we have currently company direct facility is six, then we have taken on contract. It's almost four.

items.statement: RISE business growing, adding containers monthly.
items.quote: It's going good, and we are getting a good response from our client. We are getting regular and continue order from existing client, but it is very initial stage for us in green markets.

items.statement: Top line growth of 18% to 20% for the financial year.
items.quote: Our aim for the whole financial year, again, to reiterate as we are having the call and we've crossed 2 months of the year, we'll continue to be having a top line growth of 18% to 20%, and we will try to endeavour to increase our bottom line as well, with the focus on improving the diamond sales.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 6.8% to 7.2% and PAT margin of 3.5% to 3.7%.
items.quote: And in terms of the endeavour towards profitability, I think we will be working towards having and achieving an EBITDA of anywhere between 6.8% to 7.2% and our endeavour to achieve a PAT of 3.5% to 3.7% shall continue to remain.

items.statement: Plan to add 18-20 stores, with at least 10 franchisees and 8-10 company-owned stores.
items.quote: And as far as the franchisees are concerned, we intend to add a minimum of 18 to 20 stores with a higher focus on having more and more franchisees. So minimum 10 franchisees we will be adding and about 8 to 10 company-owned company-operated stores with a strong focus, as always, we've been mentioning on East India and North India.

items.statement: Current growth in value is around 18% to 19% as of end-May.
items.quote: So I think even though the gold prices are close to their all -time high, the faith and the trust of consumers towards the commodity gold and silver have been strong, and consumers are looking for an opportunity whenever they can buy or the prices are something of within their range. They want to and are planning to buy the jewellery.

items.statement: Stud ratio target of 15% in 3 to 4 years.
items.quote: Stud ratio has given a range bound, and it has grown very significantly in Q4, and we are hopeful and confident that with the growing interest, the stud ratio, which we have been looking for a 15% range in 3 to 4 years, we'll achieve that.

items.statement: Gold Metal Loan rates increased but expected to have no significant impact.
items.quote: However, we are confident that the way it is shaping up, there will not be any significant impact on the Gold Metal Loan price.

items.statement: Gold price volatility may cause timing gaps in gross margin.
items.quote: In case of volatile gold prices, there may be a timing gap in the gross margin despite best of the effort, and they can move from one quarter to another.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth of 15% to 16%.
items.quote: No, just to add to what Mr. Banka said, that our same-store sales growth has continued to be in the range of 15% to 16%.

items.statement: ROCE expected to improve to 16-17% in 3-4 years.
items.quote: See, we are looking at 16% to 17% in the next 3 to 4 years, right?

items.statement: Additional working capital requirement of INR 300-400 crore.
items.quote: We are currently looking at an additional working capital requirement of approximately INR 300 to INR 400 crore.

items.statement: Diamond volume growth target of 15% to 20%.
items.quote: So on a safe level, a maximum 15% to 20% diamond growth we can look at, which will purely be driven by the volume.

items.statement: Plan to add 3-4 more Everlite stores out of 20.
items.quote: So that way focus will also be Everlite. You can look at 3 to 4 more Everlite stores out of 20.

items.statement: Preliminary FY26 guidance: 20% growth in gross margin and 30% growth in EBITDA.
items.value: 20% growth in revenue less service cost; 30% growth in EBITDA
items.quote: For FY '26, we are introducing preliminary guidance of 20% growth in revenue less service cost or our gross margin and 30% growth in EBITDA.

items.statement: Expects corporate and B2B to be 65-70% of gross bookings next fiscal year.
items.quote: And on a next fiscal year basis, we expect our corporate and B2B business to be between 65% to 70% of our overall gross bookings.

items.statement: Expects gradual growth in B2C business starting Q2 of current fiscal year.
items.quote: Based on the current trends, we expect to start seeing gradual growth in our B2C business in the second quarter of the current fiscal year.

items.statement: Expects air volume growth close to 15%.
items.quote: The volume increase would be closer to 15%, Anmol, the reason being because the mix of hotels which are higher yielding and more profitable is also going up in the business. So from an air volume point of view, air volumes, we would expect them to grow clo ser to 15

items.statement: Expects hotels and packages gross margin growth ~25%, air ~15%.
items.quote: Out of the gross margin growth that we have, we will expect hotels and packages growth to be closer to about 25%, and we will expect Air growth to be closer to 15%.

items.statement: Aims for 50-50 mix between air and hotels/packages in 3 years.
items.quote: So, on a blended overall business basis, we want to get to a stage in the next 3 years, where we have at least a 50-50 mix, which is there between air and hotels and packages.

items.statement: Globe margin synergies to add INR1-1.5 crores per quarter, playing out in current quarter.
items.value: INR1 crores to INR1.5 crores a quarter
items.quote: So, in terms of profit, I think the incremental synergies will add about INR1 crores to INR1.5 crores a quarter, somewhere in that kind of a range.

items.statement: Customer acquisition cost expected to trend 2.6-3%.
items.quote: So if I was to model it, right, we are modeling it between 2.6% and 3%. That's why we would look at this going forward.

items.statement: B2C airline discounts median 3.5-4.5% for the quarter.
items.quote: But if I was to average out the quarter, it would be, the median would be between 3.5% to 4.5%.

items.statement: MICE business has seasonality; Q2 and Q3 are higher quarters.
items.quote: One, our MICE business has a certain amount of seasonality. The second quarter and third quarter are typically higher quarters for the MICE business followed by Q4 and Q1.

items.statement: Expects cash flow from operations positive in current year.
items.quote: So from a cash flow from operations, including changes in working capital, in the current year, we expect to be positive.

items.statement: SaaS opportunity expected INR10-15 crores bottom line in 3-4 years.
items.quote: I would expect this to be in terms of bottom line contribution, right, about, it's between INR10 crores to INR15 crores, right?

items.statement: Expense management and card solutions could contribute one third of income in 3-5 years.
items.quote: And if I look at this 3 to 5 years down the road, I do think that from an income point of view, one third of our income could potentially come from these, and the expense management solution could be not just an India -focused solution but will be a combination of India plus international markets.

items.statement: Merger of subsidiaries expected to complete by end of August; tax savings INR4-5 million per quarter.
items.value: INR4 million to INR5 million a quarter
items.quote: So, we would expect this to get completed sometime around the August time frame, right? So, by end of August, we would expect this to be completed. And if I look at from an expense point of view, our current tax outflow is in the range of about INR4 million to INR5 million a quarter.

items.statement: Working capital of INR250-300 crores could be freed up over next few years via credit card solution.
items.quote: So on that 21 days effectively means about INR250 crores to INR300 crores of working capital that can be freed up over the next few years.

items.statement: Expects 18-20% revenue growth for FY26.
items.quote: We are expecting around 18%-20% growth.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin around 36% for FY26.
items.quote: We expect it to close around 36% should be the lowest EBITDA that we achieve in this year.

items.statement: Plans capex of around Rs. 70 Cr for FY26.
items.quote: CAPEX guidance for this year again is around Rs. 70 Cr.

items.statement: Plans to add 15-18 new centers in FY26.
items.quote: So, we overall plan to add 15 -18 new centers in this fiscal year.

items.statement: Opened 5 centers in first 2 months and plans 3 more in June, totaling 8 in Q1.
items.quote: Yes, so 5 have already opened in the first 2 months that is April and May 2025 and 3 are ready to open. We are just waiting for 1 license which I expect to get any day. So therefore, we will be opening 8 centers all together in this 1st quarter.

items.statement: Plans to open 4 big and 4 small centers in the next half.
items.quote: Yes. So we are planning to open 4 big centers and 4 small centers.

items.statement: Takes price increase of around 2%-3% every alternate year.
items.quote: Price, normally we take an increase of around 2%-3% every alternate year.

items.statement: Volume of tests grew around 10% year-on-year.
items.quote: So volume of tests has been growing at around 10% for us if we compare FY '24 and FY '25.

items.statement: Bangladesh tension impacts business; 5% of patients from Bangladesh.
items.quote: It does impact our business because West Bengal has a very porous border with Bangladesh, and we have 3 centers very close to the border where we do enough business from Bangladeshi patients. We have factored in all that and therefore we are giving outer growth potential of around 18%-20% this year.

items.statement: Acquired 63% stake in Fetomat Wellness in April 2025.
items.quote: The transaction was successfully completed in April 2025, upon which the company held a 63% equity stake in Fetomat.

items.statement: Expects Fetomat to grow 20%-25% annually.
items.quote: But if you look at Fetomat, we are expecting a growth of around 20%-25% every year.

items.statement: Plans to offer fetal medicine in 4 centers initially, scaling to 12 by year-end.
items.quote: Initially we are opening it in 4 of our own centers. And by the year end, it should be almost 12 Suraksha current centers will also be doing fetal medicine.

items.statement: Expects most centers to cater to fetal medicine in 2 to 2.5 years.
items.quote: And in a period of around 2 to 2-1/2 years, we will expect most of our centers to be catering to fetal medicine.

items.statement: Brand name transfer to SDL is in process, no definitive timeline.
items.quote: Yes. The brand name we have applied for transferring it to SDL, which is still in the process

items.statement: Plans to establish MRI in Calcutta Medical College in next 90 days.
items.quote: But we are in the process of establishing MRI in Calcutta Medical College, which should happen in the next 90 days and that possibly is a very good opportunity for us.

items.statement: Targets AUM of Rs. 4,000 crores, may exceed; revenue to AUM 3%-3.5%; PAT margins maintained or exceeded.
items.quote: From an AUM of Rs. 1,572 crores, as I have demonstrated to you, we are looking to lock in an AUM of Rs. 4,000 crores. Obviously there s still a large runway in front of us and there is a very high probability we may be able to exceed that.

items.statement: On track to become global asset manager with AUM over $1 billion by 2028, may prepone to 2027.
items.quote: Not only that we are already on track to become a global asset manager with an AUM of over $1 billion by 2028, we are likely do actually prepone this event to even 2027.

items.statement: Projects similar or higher CAGR growth on revenues, PAT, EBITDA year-on-year this year and going forward.
items.quote: we project a similar or higher CAGR growth on revenues, on PAT, on EBITDA, year-on-year, in this year and going forward, given what we are already looking to close and what we have already locked in in our favor.

items.statement: Locked in Rs. 1,000 crores trades in India and Rs. 1,500+ crores assets in UAE; to add Rs. 2,500 crores AUM over next two quarters.
items.quote: We have also locked in almost Rs. 1,500 plus crores of assets in the UAE and these are, friends, in addition to what we already manage. If I add both of them, we are looking to add almost Rs. 2,500 crores of assets under management over the next two quarters, in addition to what we hold.

items.statement: Expects AUM mix to become 50-50 between UAE and India by end of this financial year.
items.quote: 29% being in the UAE and 71% being in India, we expect this to become 50-50 effectively by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: As AUM grows to Rs. 4,000 crores, fund management share likely 40%-42%, advisory about 60%.
items.quote: As we go to Rs. 4,000 crores of assets under management this year, this is likely to be more like 40%-42%, with advisory being about 60%.

items.statement: Effective tax rate likely to go from 22% to 18%-19% in current year.
items.quote: So, we are likely to go from a current 22% effective tax rate to maybe 18%-19% tax rate as well in this current year.

items.statement: Does not expect recurring expense to grow materially; revenue impact to flow into PBT and PAT.
items.quote: So, we do ot expect now this number to grow by any material amount, whereas obviously the revenue impact is where we are going to see, thereby directly flowing into our PBT and PAT going forward.

items.statement: Invested almost Rs. 20 crore into infrastructure, licenses, offices, partnerships; to be amortized over seven years.
items.quote: We have invested almost Rs. 20 crore into creating the infrastructure which I talked about, the partnership with global baniks, the distribution, the offices, the licenses across UAE, across GIFT City, actoss India. And a lot of these expenses have obviously gone to capital which are

items.statement: Has bank sanctions over $68 million, another $200 million underway; $200 million commitments under closure; total deployable corpus close to $500 million.
items.quote: We have got sanctions from one of the global banks for over $68 million with another $200 million of bank sanctions underway. We have $200 million of commitments now under closure from global funds, who are looking to participate in a UAE fund, thereby taking the total deployable corpus to close to $500 million.

items.statement: Partnerships of over $200 million potential joining global capital pool; announcements soon.
items.quote: We have got some of the largest global prominent investors who have now come on board with us and very soon you will see announcements about these partnerships of over $200 million potential which are joining hands with us in our global capital pool.

items.statement: Will be cautious in next quarter and stay away from large commitments in India markets.
items.quote: Obviously, in line with market, we will be cautious in the next quarter and stay away from making any large commitments in the India markets.

items.statement: Last quarter marked caution in real estate sector; need to exercise caution higher than last three years.
items.quote: So, the last quarter of the last financial year marked a bit of caution now appearing within the RE sector, which has so far in the last three years have scen unabated growth and demand. We see that as a growing concern We need more capital, but the need to exercise caution is now higher than the last three years.

items.statement: Revenue per employee targeted to move from Rs. 1.5 crores to Rs. 2.5 crores or beyond.
items.quote: Despite that, the revenue per employee is target to move from Rs. 1.5 crores to Rs. 2.5 crores or beyond.

items.statement: Plans to ramp up steel melting shop capacity utilization from 60% in FY25 to 75-80%.
items.quote: Primarily, we are looking at raising the capacity utilization overall from 60% of the melt up to 75%-80%. And the moment we achieve that we will look at further options.

items.statement: Aims to run TMT plant at 60-70% utilization over FY26 and FY27.
items.quote: And we definitely aspire to achieve over a 2-year scenario, FY '26 and FY '27. We are looking at running that plant at least 60%-70% utilization.

items.statement: Expects to add around Rs. 150 crores from TMT bars this year at 30-35% utilization.
items.quote: assuming that we operated about at very nominal capacity utilization this year, close to around 30%-35% also, if you assume then we should add close to around Rs. 150 crores from TMT bars this year.

items.statement: Aspires to at least maintain stainless-steel sales, if not better.
items.quote: We definitely aspire to at least remain the same if not better, right. That is what we would strive to achieve.

items.statement: Bullish on demand from NCR realty segment; plans to expand retail and target infrastructure projects.
items.quote: So, basically our target market is NCR and because of the reality boom here, the way Gurgaon, the way regions at Haryana are expanding or various projects coming up in UP, also Noida, so we are quite bullish on the demand front with respect to coming in from these basically realty segment.

items.statement: Cheaper Chinese steel imports adversely impacting domestic pricing; safeguard duty may be insufficient.
items.quote: Notably, the US’ renewed tariff or taxes, particularly against Chinese imports, are leading to an influx of cheaper Chinese steel into India, adversely impacting domestic pricing.

items.statement: Threat of dumping remains key concern if India does not implement strong trade protection measures.
items.quote: The threat of dumping remains a key concern, especially if India does not implement strong trade protection measures.

items.statement: Government initiated 12% payback duty, but it seems insufficient to safeguard industry.
items.quote: The government, as we all know, has already initiated a 12% payback duty, which at the moment doesn't seem sufficient to sort of safeguard the industry to the level that we would want to and the various steel associations are in touch with the government to further enhance the same.

items.statement: Stainless-steel hot rebars planned for pan India presence.
items.quote: In fact, stainless-steel hot rebars are going to be a pan India presence is what we are looking at.

items.statement: More than 95% of sales were stainless-steel; TMT bars to be incremental revenue.
items.quote: But I would say more than 95% of our sales would have been safely stainless-steel only. So, going forward, assuming that segment remains at the level that you are operating, also as have said that we want to increase the capacity utilization there as well, we are operating about 60%, which we want to increase.

items.statement: Recommenced TMT mill operations to utilize idle assets and improve brand visibility.
items.quote: We recently announced recommencement of commercial operations of our TMT mill division, which was remaining idle for a few years. This facility is dedicated to the production of TMT bars, which is a key component in construction activities.

items.statement: Received BIS license for 8-32 mm stainless-steel rebars and mild steel TMT bars.
items.quote: On another note, we have received a license from BIS covering the entire range from 8 mm to 32 mm, which will make roll out of our stainless-steel rebars more effective. We have also received a similar license for the mild steel TMT bars which allows us to service a large number of customers in North India for these product categories.

items.statement: Implemented cost and energy optimization including billet charging facility for stainless-steel billets to wire rods.
items.quote: Aligned with the sustainability goals, we implemented cost and energy optimization initiatives including a billet charging facility of stainless-steel billets to wire rods making us the only company in the country to be doing so currently.

items.statement: Took temporary shutdown of steel melting shop in April 2025 for revamping; operations resumed with better efficiency.
items.quote: Recently, in April 2025, we also took a shutdown, a temporary shutdown, for about a couple of weeks for our steel melting shop at Ghaziabad, which was carried out essentially for revamping and refurbishment and replacement of certain critical equipments.

items.statement: No inventory gains; better realizations from spread between raw materials and finished products and cost savings.
items.quote: No, there is no inventory gain. There is no sort of any exceptional number, the markets have been more or less stable, the prices, rather the steel prices have been soft overall last year.

items.statement: Plans to add 22,000 to 25,000 seats in leasing at average rental of INR6,500 to INR7,000 with 90% occupancy.
items.quote: So as you know, that we are looking at adding anything between 22,000 to 25,000 seats on the leasing business going forward at an average rate, anything between INR6,500 to INR7,000 rental and maintaining 90% occupancy.

items.statement: Expects design and build business to grow at least 60% to 70% year-on-year.
items.quote: And as we have in past, explained that we are certainly expecting under this business to grow at least by 60% to 70% year-on-year.

items.statement: Targets 50% to 60% capacity utilization in furniture business this financial year.
items.quote: And in terms of furniture business, as I've explained that the total capacity in value terms is about INR275 crores to INR300 crores, and we are looking at achieving anything around 50% to 60% capacity utilization this financial year.

items.statement: Design and build order book is INR200 crores plus, including a large MNC contract of INR183 crores.
items.quote: And in terms of order book, we have confirmed orders of INR200 crores plus while we are talking in the first quarter of this new financial year, we have made an announcement already to that impact that in fact that there's a large contract from an MNC client we have received for INR183 crores.

items.statement: Furniture division has a current order book of about INR35 crores.
items.quote: Our manufacturing capacity at present is about INR275 crores to INR300 crores in value terms with a current order book of about INR35 crores.

items.statement: Received a significant contract from a Middle East resort company valued around INR25 crores.
items.quote: And in fact, I would like to also update you that we have got a significant contract from a resort company in the Middle East for whom we are going to deliver this furniture, which is valued roughly around INR25 crores.

items.statement: Capex for leasing business is about INR50,000 per seat, with around 10% invested by the company.
items.quote: But if you look at overall on an average basis, let's say, if I'm on an average leasing out on an annual basis, about 20,000 to 25,000 seat s, my capex is about INR50,000 per seat. And let's say, around 10% thereof is something that we kind of keep -- we invest ourselves

items.statement: No major capex planned in furniture vertical this financial year.
items.quote: And this financial year, we are not looking at any further investment as of now.

items.statement: Design and build segment margins on average range between 17% to 20%.
items.quote: In terms of overall margins, if I talk about our margins in this segment on an average ranges between 17% to 20%, 22%.

items.statement: Leasing business EBITDA margin is about 30% on average.
items.quote: So the such margins, as we typically discuss in our leasing business, on an EBITDA level, we make about on an average, 30% in the pure leasing businesses.

items.statement: Offering price is between INR6,500 to INR7,500 per seat, with gradual rental increases.
items.quote: If you look at us, then our offering is between INR6,500 to INR7,500. And our other product is Sprint.

items.statement: Average capacity utilization is about 90% plus across core assets.
items.quote: Yes, sir. Yes. So I mean, as we have always mentioned that our average capacity utilization is about 90% plus. And all our core assets at this point of time are operating at 90% plus capacities.

items.statement: Not looking at any capital raise due to healthy debt-equity ratio of 0.335%.
items.quote: At present, in terms of the capital raise, certainly, we are not looking at any capital raise because we are still maintaining a healthy debt-equity ratio. It's just about 0.335% and we still have leverage potential there.

items.statement: Working capital cycle ranges 15-25 days for leasing and 45-60 days for furniture and design and build.
items.quote: depending upon -- if you look at the overall cycle, it ranges around 15 to 20 / 25 days from the leasing business. While if you look at the furniture business and the design and build business, that ranges between 45 to 60 days

items.statement: REIT IPO expected in FY26 after legal due diligence.
items.quote: One thing is that the legal DD is in progress on the property we have identified. And once the legal DD is cleared, then maybe we will announce it for the IPO process.

items.statement: Refrains from volume and margin guidance for FY26 due to tariff uncertainty.
items.quote: Given the fluid nature of the current tariff situation, with a 90 -day pause period set to conclude by early July, we believe it is prudent to refrain from volume and margin guidance for FY '26 at this point of time.

items.statement: Confident in doubling revenue by 2028.
items.quote: As of FY '25, Indo Count has achieved revenues of approximately $500 million, and we remain confident and committed to our goal of doubling our revenue by 2028.

items.statement: North Carolina greenfield phase 1 investment INR130 crores, INR99 crores pending, completion by September 2025.
items.quote: So our total investment, we have invested so far INR31 crores. The total investment is INR130 crores in first phase. So INR99 crores is pending, which will be done between April of this year to September.

items.statement: Peak revenue potential from North Carolina phase 1 is US$85-90 million; total utility bedding business $175 million.
items.quote: And for the North Carolina specific facility, the revenue expectation is between US$85 million to US$90 million. And for the utility bedding business, all put together is $175 million.

items.statement: Expects 150-200 bps margin impact for next 12-18 months from US investments.
items.quote: So, of course, for our utility bedding and brand business, it's -- we've created a full infrastructure in the US, whether it's showroom, whether it's talent, of course, all these manufacturing facilities, which we have said even in our previous call that, that has a 150 to 200 basis point impact for the next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: Targets overall margin of 16-17% once businesses stabilize.
items.quote: And overall, we maintain that as an organization, we would like to do between 16% to 17% margin across the board.

items.statement: Average selling price impacted by approximately 6% due to down trading.
items.quote: This resulted in both volume and value down trading, which impacted our average selling price by approximately 6% compared to the average of the previous few quarters.

items.statement: Similar volume and value trend in Q1 FY26, expecting gradual improvement thereafter.
items.quote: We continue to witness similar volume and value trend in Q1 FY '26 and expect subsequent quarters thereon to improve gradually.

items.statement: Product mix shifted to lower to mid-priced offerings due to reduced consumer confidence.
items.quote: This shift in sentiment altered our product mix , with increased demand skewing towards lower to mid-priced offerings as opposed to our typical sales profile.

items.statement: Short-term demand impacted by consumer confidence and sourcing strategies.
items.quote: As we move into the next financial year, we anticipate short -term demand to be impacted by consumer confidence and overall sourcing strategy of our end customers.

items.statement: Invested INR460 crores in brand acquisitions, capacity expansion, brand building, and talent acquisition.
items.quote: Over the past 12 to 15 months, we have invested approximately INR460 crores in brand acquisitions, capacity expansion, brand building and talent acquisition, thus laying the foundation for a future -ready diversified product portfolio.

items.statement: Expects interest cost around INR120-130 crores annually.
items.quote: So overall, I think the interest cost will be around INR120 crores, INR130 crores annually.

items.statement: Expects better flow-through from EBITDA to PAT by 150 basis points over next 2 years.
items.quote: As we scale our volumes and revenues, we expect better flow -through from EBITDA to PAT over the next 2 years.

items.statement: New segments and brands contributed INR125 crores in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: But our new segments, which is utility bedding and our new brands, which is Fieldcrest, Waverly, (Wamsutta has not started in Q4 ) contributed to INR125 crores in revenue, out of the revenue of INR1,029 crores, INR125 crores has come from there.

items.statement: Plans to launch Wamsutta as direct-to-consumer brand within 30-60 days.
items.quote: So we expect to launch it within the next 30 to 60 days as a direct -to -consumer brand.

items.statement: Targeting Rs. 2,000 crores pre-sales for FY26.
items.quote: We are targeting for Rs. 2,000 crores internally again for this year.

items.statement: Expects top line around Rs. 1,200 crores in FY26.
items.quote: We would expect around Rs. 1,200 crores of top line this year.

items.statement: Senior living pre-sales to cross Rs. 450 crores this year.
items.quote: And this year, we are looking to cross Rs. 450 crores of pre-sales in senior living.

items.statement: Plans to launch three new projects this year.
items.quote: We plan to launch Ashiana Amaya in Jamshedpur as well this year. We are working to get Jaisingpura also launched in Jaipur. So, we hope to launch about three projects like that.

items.statement: Aaroham launch in Q3, Jaisingpura in Q4.
items.quote: So, Aaroham in Q3, Aaroham and Amaya in Q3, and New Land Jaisingpura in Q4 of this year.

items.statement: Aaroham total saleable area around 11 lakh sq ft, launching a third in first phase.
items.quote: Around 11 lakh square foot total I think we should launch a third of that in the first phase.

items.statement: Expects to maintain Rs. 2,000 crores bookings for FY26 and FY27.
items.quote: I think so, with Aaroham coming in Gurgaon, that would have, yes, the idea is to maintain that basis that, yes.

items.statement: Plans to launch all projects within this year to deliver by FY30.
items.quote: And my view is that we need to launch all of these within this year, and then work hard to make sure we can deliver this by FY '30.

items.statement: Expects ROE to cross 15% in FY26 on reported basis.
items.quote: I would expect so, we need to crunch the numbers, yes. So the economic basis we have crossed.

items.statement: FY26 will be last year of low margins; margins to improve in FY27 and FY28.
items.quote: This year the margins will, it's the '27 and '28 when we see margins significantly improve. '26 we will have quarters with good margins.

items.statement: Cumulative profit target of Rs. 2,000 crores on Rs. 11,000 crores sales, 18-19% margin.
items.quote: we have talked about our total book including these running to about Rs. 11,000 crores of sales and about Rs. 2,000 crores of profit, so that would be 18%, 19% kind of after-tax margin.

items.statement: Estimated 14-15% margins on sold but unrecognized revenue of Rs. 4,500 crores.
items.quote: I would sort of estimate about 14%, 15% of margins on a blended basis across the same.

items.statement: No pricing pressures in any market; sales comfortable.
items.quote: There are no pricing pressures anywhere in any market. We are not concerned with sale prices in any market at this point of time.

items.statement: Land prices unsustainable in some micro-markets like Jaipur.
items.quote: To me, land prices are unsustainable in some micro -markets. Because they are factoring in a much different price as compared to the price points we are selling at overall.

items.statement: Amarah Phase-1 delivery pushed to FY27 due to NCR construction bans.
items.quote: What is happening in NCR now is, if you are not able to get things ready by October and have our OC applied for it, be ready to take out checklists by then, then the delay is not 15 days, if I delay 15, 20 days, then the delay goes actually three, four months because we lose about two and a half months now to NGT construction bans during that time.

items.statement: No buyback due to tax inefficiency.
items.quote: Buybacks have become very tax inefficient for shareholders.

items.statement: Expects 15-20% turnover growth this year.
items.quote: And we are expecting at least 15% -- 15% to 20% jump in the turnover of this year. But again, this depend upon the -- how the project execution goes.

items.statement: Order book at all-time high of INR11,700 crores as of March 31, 2025.
items.quote: Company's order book position has reached its all-time high in financial year '24, '25 and stands at INR11,700 crores as on 31st March 2025 as compared to INR7,823 crores as on 31st March 2024.

items.statement: Order inflow increased to INR8,214 crores in FY25.
items.quote: Order inflow in EIL has increased significantly to INR8,214 crores in financial year '24, '25 as compared to the order inflow of INR3,400 crores in financial year '23, '24.

items.statement: Aims to sustain order inflow at similar level and grow further.
items.quote: We can assess to sustain the existing order value. We will -- the order inflow, what we have got in this financial year we will try to sustain the same and we'll further grow from the existing order book -- sorry, order inflow.

items.statement: Already booked INR1,300 crores worth of business as of now.
items.quote: For your information, as of today, we have already booked INR1,300 crores worth of business. And then the second year is -- in the second market, sir.

items.statement: Will maintain similar profit margins going forward.
items.quote: And with respect to the profit margins, we are going to maintain the similar profit margins so we are quite capable of.

items.statement: Targets normal margins of 25% in consultancy and 5-7% in LSTK.
items.quote: But definitely, for the future, we are targeting in the normal range of 25% and 5% to 7% in LSTK business.

items.statement: Consultancy to be 50-60% of order inflow, LSTK the balance.
items.quote: Consultancy would be a little bit more than the LSTK so always remain in the range of 50%, 55%, 55%, 60% is consultancy and balance is LSTK.

items.statement: No major capex in pipeline; only routine capex.
items.quote: Capex is the routine in nature around the building for the renovations asset. So there is no major capex is in pipeline.

items.statement: Hydrocarbon business expected to continue for at least next decade.
items.quote: So we don't see any major difference in the hydrocarbon business from all these segments. So that is going to be there for at least next decade or so.

items.statement: Expects same level of other income next year.
items.quote: In this financial year, we got the dividend of INR12 crores to INR13 crores from the NRL, and we are expecting the same level of other income in the coming next year.

items.statement: RFCL may declare dividend in current year.
items.quote: As far as dividend is concerned, last year -- in the current year, we have got the dividend of INR12 crores from the NRL and RFCL is still to declare -- still to start declaring dividend, and we are expecting that in the current year, RFCL may declare some dividend for the investor.

items.statement: No further investment planned in NRL and RFCL.
items.quote: In the NRL, we have already completed all the investment cycle, and there is no further planned investment in the RFCL as well as NRL, we have already subscribed to the right issue of NRL that has been completed.

items.statement: Success ratio around 25-35% in competitive scenario.
items.quote: Success ratio, you can say around 25% to 30%, 35% competitive scenario.

items.statement: Payment terms 30 days, average collection around 40-45 days.
items.quote: Generally, our payment terms are 30 days, and most of the payments we are receiving in 30 days. On an average, it comes to around 40 days.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book of around 325 to 330 crores to be executed over next 24 to 36 months.
items.quote: We have an unexecuted order book of around 325 to 330 crores, and all these projects have to be executed over the next 24 to 36 months.

items.statement: Looking to build up an order book around 250 to 300 crores during the year.
items.quote: In addition to that, we are looking at building up an order book around 250 to 300 crores during the year.

items.statement: Looking at operations margins of 8 to 10%.
items.quote: But other than that, we would be looking at operations of 8 to 10%. That is, typically the margin we would be looking at.

items.statement: Looking at raising around 8,200 crores in the QIP.
items.quote: We are looking at raising somewhere around 8,200 crores in the queue.

items.statement: Got shareholder approvals to raise money through QIP route and got limits from certain bankers.
items.quote: We have already got shareholder approvals to raise money through the QIP route. In addition to that we have already got limits from certain bankers, and there are some legacy arbitration issues which are being sorted out.

items.statement: Will reduce promoter holding to 90% by doing OFS.
items.quote: So that process is in ongoing process, and we will be reducing a holding to 90% by doing OFS.

items.statement: Have another 2 years to bring promoter holding down from 90 to 75%.
items.quote: So, we will be following that regulation, and that gives us another 2 years’ time to bring it down from 90 to 75%.

items.statement: Expecting significant headway towards receiving Bihar arbitration claim in next 3 to 4 months.
items.quote: So, in the next 3 to 4 months, we are expecting significant headway towards receiving this particular claim.

items.statement: NHAI arbitration to start middle of June and should be over within this year.
items.quote: In May 2025, which is last month, the Supreme Court has again started the arbitration, and middle of June the arbitration is going to start, and | think it should be over by within this year.

items.statement: Tax outgo for next few years would be extremely minimal due to huge tax shield.
items.quote: If you will see, there's a very little tax, because primarily this company has a huge tax shield and tax outgo for the next few years would be extremely minimal.

items.statement: PBT and PAT are more or less the same due to large tax shield.
items.quote: And we have a large tax shield. So, our PBT and PAT are more or less the same.

items.statement: Top line would continue to grow in the future.
items.quote: This is a strong momentum, and this top line would continue to grow in the future.

items.statement: Looking at consistent profit in the coming times.
items.quote: So, we are looking at consistent profit in the coming times.

items.statement: Process of injecting working capital has started and looking forward to raising some working capital in coming months.
items.quote: The process of injecting working capital has already started, and we are looking forward to raising some working capital in the coming months.

items.statement: Looking at raising new working capital lines through bank facilities or QIP.
items.quote: However, going forward, we are looking at raising new working capital lines, which may be through various mechanisms of getting bank facilities or from QIP related QIP or similar issues.

items.statement: Financial restructuring ongoing, fruits would be out over next couple of months.
items.quote: It is still undergoing, and I think, over the next couple of months the fruits of this financial restructuring would be out.

items.statement: Targeting 20-25 cars per month run rate within FY26, doubling to 40-50 cars per month in FY27.
items.value: 20-25 cars per month, 40-50 cars per month
items.quote: We are quite hopeful and confident that we will be able to achieve the run rate of between 20 to 25 cars a month within the financial year. And all the facilities are set up, and once the Vande Bharat production also comes in stream, we will be able to enhance this to double of that, which we expect to be able to do in FY '27, where our target would be to get to a run rate of between 40 to 50 cars

items.statement: Targeting 125-150 traction motors per month in FY26, up from 50 per month last year.
items.quote: We are now targeting to ramp this up to between 125 to 150 traction motors per month. So that is 1,500 to 1,800 traction motors per month from this financial year itself.

items.statement: Foundry expansion to reach 40,000 tonnes castings monthly run rate within FY26.
items.quote: We are targeting, in the first phase, to get to around 40,000 tonnes of castings, which we are confident of being able to achieve on a monthly run rate basis within the current financial year.

items.statement: First Gujarat Metro train expected in Q2 FY26; Vande Bharat in end Q4 FY26 or early Q1 FY27.
items.period: Q2 FY26, Q4 FY26, Q1 FY27
items.quote: We are expecting the first train of Gujarat Metro, that is Ahmedabad Metro, to be done in Q2 of the current financial year. And the Vande Bharat is expected in end of Q4 or beginning of Q1 of the next financial year.

items.statement: Wheelset JV contractual delivery to start June 2026.
items.quote: As far as the wheelset is concerned, the contractual delivery is supposed to start from June 2026, and we are very much well in track to be able to achieve that.

items.statement: First EMU propulsion set to be supplied in Q1 or early Q2 FY26.
items.quote: We are expecting and are confident that the first set of propulsion, which is the EMU propulsion, will be supplied within Q1 of this financial year or the beginning of Q2 of the financial year.

items.statement: Targeting 800-850 cars per annum and 200-250 traction motors per month by 2027-28.
items.value: 800-850 cars per annum, 200-250 traction motors per month
items.quote: In the first phase, which we are expecting, since you were asking from a timeline of 2027-28, so we are targeting to achieve a target of 800 to 850 cars per annum, and about 200 to 250 traction motors per month. So about 3,000 traction motors per month.

items.statement: Wheelset production to normalize from June, improving wagon production.
items.quote: We understand that from the month of June, that is the current month, the production of Rail Wheel Factory will get normalized. And going forward, this problem should not be existing.

items.statement: Private sector wagon demand dampened by moratorium on wagon investment scheme; awaiting reopening.
items.quote: So the market is aware that there was a moratorium that was put on the wagon investment scheme, which has actually dampened the private sector offtake over the last few quarters. This moratorium, we believe, should not last for long, because there is a lot of appetite from the private sector to buy wagons.

items.statement: Expects new railway tenders by end of year to provide visibility for coming years.
items.quote: In terms of the order book, we have an order book which is, at our targeted production, will see us through for this current financial year. And we expect that by the end of the year, the new tenders should come up and will give us visibility for the coming years as well.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 10.4% in Q4 from 9.44%.
items.quote: We have an EBITDA margin of about 10% in this quarter. So in fact, it's a positive trend. From 9.44%, it has gone up to 10.4%.

items.statement: Titagarh Firema situation developing; potential non-cash loss quantified, limited to book value.
items.quote: So as far as Titagarh Firema is concerned, first, I would like to clarify whatever has been mentioned in the notes to our accounts, it is a situation which is still developing. We still do not have clarity as to which way the situation is going to develop. But we are watching the situation with great care and caution. Whatever was the investment made, a substantial part of it was already earlier p

items.statement: FY26 and FY27 seen as transformative years for passenger rail and new businesses.
items.quote: I would say FY '26 and then FY '27 are 2 very, very critical transformative years for the company, because historically, as also was the name of the company was a wagon company. Wagon is a stable commoditized business.

items.statement: Shipbuilding strategy, CAPEX plan, and business plan to be finalized in next few months.
items.quote: We believe that within the next few months, we will be able to finalize and come back to the market as to what the final strategy, CAPEX plan and the business plan for the shipbuilding and maritime systems would be.

items.statement: Propulsion business potential: INR 300-400 crores from traction motors, INR 500-1000 crores from EMU/MEMU, total INR 1500 crores.
items.quote: We believe that we can easily look at doing approximately 2,000 traction motors a year, which will give us a revenue of about INR 300 crores to INR 400 crores. And as far as the EMU/MEMU and other propulsion systems for the railway is concerned, this should be another about INR 500 crores, INR 700 crores to INR 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Wagon capacity 12,000 per year, potential revenue INR 4000-4500 crores.
items.quote: So as far as the segments are concerned, the Freight Business segment, we have a capacity of doing 12,000 wagons a year, which if we look at just extrapolating the sales number can give us a potential revenue of around INR 4,000 crores, INR 4,500 crores.

items.statement: Targets INR 1,500 crores annual revenue from Dyes and Intermediates segment.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect margin improvements as legal costs decline and anticipate INR 1,500 crores of annual revenue from our Dyes and Intermediates segment.

items.statement: Expects 8-10% EBITDA margin on INR 1,500 crores revenue.
items.quote: Well, if we assume that the legal cost is going to go down, which is happening now with a lot of legal work is getting co mpleted with the sale purchase agreement signed, we should be having at least 8% to 10% EBITDA on

items.statement: Plans to invest INR 8,000 crores in new copper and fertilizer project over 2-2.5 years.
items.quote: So over a period of next 2 to 2.5 years, company is going to invest something close to INR 8,000 crores in a new project.

items.statement: New copper and fertilizer project to generate INR 45,000 crores annual revenue.
items.quote: But over a period of the next 2 to 3 years, we will be investing somewhere close to INR 8,000 crores in CAPEX, and which will generate, as I mentioned, almost INR 45,000 crores of revenue on the full operation basis of the copper and fertilizer facility.

items.statement: Copper segment to have 8-12% EBITDA margin due to value-added products and new technology.
items.quote: See, the margins are coming from 2 major factors. Number one, company is investing into manufacturing of copper, including value-added products.

items.statement: Copper concentrate sourcing is challenging; 50% tied up, aiming for 100% in 6-12 months.
items.quote: With certain contracts which we have executed till now, we are at 50% tie-up from Chile, Africa and Peru, but we are still 50% away, and it will still take us another 6 months to a year before we have 100% or 125% of our requirement is fully tied up with offtake agreements.

items.statement: Expects INR 5,200-5,300 crores post-tax from DyStar stake sale.
items.quote: Yes, INR 5,200 crores to INR 5,300 crores, correct. That's a fair assumption.

items.statement: DyStar deal expected to close by October 2, 2025, with possible 30-day extension.
items.quote: The deal is expected to close by October 2, 2025, subject to condition s precedents from the sale, which will be strategically deployed for a new investments and shareholder

items.statement: Plans to reward shareholders from DyStar proceeds.
items.quote: Yes. Yes, yes. As we have informed earlier, there would be certain parts which will be rewarding to the shareholders, yes.

items.statement: Legal expenses expected to halve from June onwards, reducing to INR 7-8 crores per quarter.
items.quote: Yes. Yes, yes. Of course, from this month onwards, from June onwards, we are actually expecting the legal expenses to go half.

items.statement: QCO enforcement from August 13 to positively impact dye intermediate prices.
items.quote: And for h-acid and vinyl sulphone, it was to start from May 13, but the government has extended it for 3 more months. So August 13 is the exact date on which the QCO would be enforced in India for dyes and intermediates.

items.statement: Plans to improve product mix and increase capacity utilization to drive revenue growth.
items.quote: Our current capacities are underutilized. We are utilizing only 42% capacity of entire installed capacity of Kiri on stand-alone basis on all plants. So we will be ramping up our capacities, and ramping up with value-added products with improvement of product mix.

items.statement: JV expected to make EBITDA of INR 150-200 crores.
items.quote: JV will make EBITDA somewhere in the range of INR 150 crores to INR 200 crores.

items.statement: Interested in buying out partner's 60% stake in Lonsen Kiri.
items.quote: We have already tried, we attempted. We sent a proposal to the partner on the other side. But I think it would be a separate negotiation. We would be 100% interested to buy out the partner stake in Lonsen Kiri.

items.statement: If Longsheng fails to close by October 2, deal may go to second bidder by December 31.
items.quote: So I don't think receiver is going to wait, because let us say, if Longsheng fails on October 2, receiver has to close it by December 31, because December 31 is called long stop date, it cannot extend beyond it.

items.statement: Looking forward to do 12,000 metric tons minimum for FY26.
items.quote: So on the volume front, we are looking forward to do the 12,000 metric tons minimum for the FY '26.

items.statement: No additional investment planned next year except power backup and efficiency improvements.
items.quote: Not in the next year. Right now, there are no plans for additional investment, except for some power backup systems and all that more to look on efficiency factors to improvise the efficiency and the cost with regard to reducing energy costs or basically, mainly any investment which is going to be done in the next | year is mainly to improvise the efficiencies in the existing capacities, mainly fo

items.statement: Expect 30-50% growth in EU in first year post approval, adding 2,500 MT.
items.quote: Well, we will be able to grow at least minimum 30% to 50% in the first 1 year of approval. That is how confident we are based on our relationships and how the overall market demand in the EU is happening.

items.statement: Ready-to-eat realization 10-15% better, additional margins $0.40-$0.50 per kilo.
items.quote: We look at a better realization for sure, that will be increasing almost — we look at it, almost 10% to 15% better realization part minimum, but at the same time, we also have to look at the additional costs which are involved for doing those products.

items.statement: Uncertainties from US tariffs expected to clear by end of Q1 or early Q2.
items.period: end of Q1 or early Q2
items.quote: We expect that such uncertainties should be cleared off by the end of Q1. We expect that, especially with regard to the trade deal announcements and all that.

items.statement: Farmgate prices corrected 8-10% post-tariff announcement.
items.quote: Roughly around 8% to 10% reduction was there. I mean roughly - let us say it is currently sitting around 7% to 8% lesser compared to what it was in the month of March to now, roughly, I'm just saying.

items.statement: Customers continuing to buy at 10% tariff, planning programs for late 2025 and early 2026.
items.quote: The customers are continuing to buy at this - considering that the tariff rates will be at 10%. But post-90 days, we need to see how the trade deal is going to happen.

items.statement: Aim to reduce dependence on any single market to 50% or less.
items.quote: We want to push it out. As I stated over a period of time in the next few years, we want to restrict even our number one market to 50% or lesser than 50%.

items.statement: EU approval for new facility expected soon, enabling RTE production.
items.quote: We expect ours also to be done very soon unlike the past when it was very uncertain. Now in that regard, certainties have improved as they started approving or actually listing out all the facilities one after the other, since March and April month, they have started approving all the facilities in India.

items.statement: No specific margin guidance for FY26 yet; wait until end of Q1.
items.quote: But on the margin front, I'l not be wanting to give you any specific guidance at this point immediately, but I would rather want to wait more for the end of the first quarter.

items.statement: Farmers positive, stocking again, seed sales improving.
items.quote: We find them to be okay. They are going for stocking again. We see our seed sales improving. It is also going in a positive manner.

items.statement: Average purchase cost INR358 per kilo in Q4 FY25, down 4% QoQ.
items.quote: Our average purchase cost of raw materials was INR358 per kilo in Q4 of FY '25, representing a 4% decrease quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: UK FTA expected to increase sales to at least 10% in first year.
items.quote: So we can definitely take it up to at least minimum 10% in the first year. I mean given whenever the FTA gets fully implemented.

items.statement: US tariffs at 10% currently, affecting Q1 FY26.
items.quote: As you know that it's kind of a global trade war-like situation because of these reciprocal tariffs which have been levied by U.S.A., which are currently at 10%, which are there affecting in the Q! from the Q1 of FY 26, which you asked specifically.

items.statement: RTE capacity 10,000 MT annually, awaiting EU approval.
items.quote: Yes. So those, that production ready-to-cat production lines, especially are to the tune of around 10,000 metric tons on an annual basis.

items.statement: EU sales grew 70% YoY in Q4 FY25, 41% in FY25.
items.quote: The company achieved a year-on-year sales growth of 70% in Q4 FY '25 and 41% in the full fiscal year of FY '25.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY26 is INR250 crores, implying 20-25% growth over FY25, excluding Shotgun.
items.quote: On the top line, and this is not including the Shotgun product launch. That will be on top. So my revenue guidance for this financial year is about INR 250 crores.

items.statement: Company targets 15-20% CAGR growth year-on-year.
items.quote: We're looking to grow at a CAGR of 15% to 20% year-on-year. And therefore, our outlook remains consistent with that.

items.statement: Aspires to deliver 20-25% year-on-year growth as a company with diversified revenue streams.
items.quote: But as a company with diversifie d revenues streams is where we believe we want to, we aspire to deliver 20% to 25% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 expected under INR15 crores, excluding hospitality project.
items.quote: We expect that number for this financial year to be under INR15 -odd crores for this fina ncial year. So nothing major. Last year, we were approximately INR40-odd crores that we spent. This year, it should be about INR15 crores.

items.statement: Gross margins improved by 200 basis points year-on-year.
items.quote: Gross margins improved by 200 basis points year -on-year driven by an enhanced product mix and operational efficiencies.

items.statement: Brand investments were 8% of top line in FY25, up from 6% previous year, expected to reduce by at least 100 bps in FY26.
items.quote: Our brand investments in FY '25 went to about 8% of our top line from 6% in the previous year. We do not wish to slow down on this.

items.statement: Gross margins at about 79% and expected to remain consistent in coming years.
items.quote: We're operating at about 79% and we believe that's a good figure which we want to remain consistent with in the years to come as well.

items.statement: Brand investments to stabilize around 5% to 6% by 2028 or 2030.
items.quote: Ultimately, as you approach 2028 or 2030, this will ultimately stabilize around 5% to 6%.

items.statement: Robust recovery in Q1 and expected to continue this year.
items.quote: With respect to demand, we've seen a robust recovery in Q1, and we see that continuing this year as well going forward.

items.statement: 73% of FY25 revenue from Premium & Above segment.
items.quote: In FY '25, 73% of our revenue was contributed by the Premium & Above segment, reinforcing our strong brand positioning and the shift in consumer preference towards our quality offerings.

items.statement: Premium range wines growing at 15% CAGR over last few years.
items.quote: Our premium range of wines have been growing at a CAGR of 15% over last few years.

items.statement: FTA with EU provides sufficient protection to domestic wines; no impact expected.
items.quote: That FTA provides sufficient pro tection to domestic wines. I don't see any impact of the FTA at this point of time.

items.statement: No compelling commercial reason to import bulk wines into India.
items.quote: But at this point of time, there is no compelling commercial reason to import bulk wines into India. We don't see it.

items.statement: Evaluating merger of holdco with Fratelli to save costs.
items.quote: We are evaluating it, yes.

items.statement: No definitive plans to raise money from market.
items.quote: We don't rule out any options, but I cannot tell you of any definitive plans today of raising money.

items.statement: Hospitality project still in planning stage, aiming to open in 2027.
items.quote: We are still in planning stage. We haven't yet begun construction. We are still very much attempting to have the facility ready by and open in 2027.

items.statement: Expects about 20% AUM growth from current base.
items.quote: I think we can look at about 20% kind of the growth from the current base. That's the number that will work out.

items.statement: Disbursements to be roughly equal to AUM size.
items.quote: I think the disbursement number will also be in line with roughly about the AUM size only. Given that most of the disbursement happened towards the second half of the financial year, which is what we have tried to explain in the PPT on Slide #12, so, more or less, equal amount of disbursement is what we will have to do.

items.statement: Targets loan officer productivity of Rs. 1.1 crores by end of FY26.
items.quote: We would like to increase productivity and efficiencies at branches and expect to improve our loan officer productivity to about Rs. 1.1 crores per loan officer by end of FY ‘26 from the current Rs. 0.6 crores at end of FY ‘25.

items.statement: Targets borrowers per loan officer to 340 by end of FY26.
items.quote: Our target in current financial year will be to improve borrowers to LO count to about 340 borrowers from the current 228 number.

items.statement: Expects situation to normalize by Q2 FY26.
items.quote: We are optimistic that the situation should normalize by the second quarter of this financial year.

items.statement: Expects profitability to improve from Q3 FY26 onwards.
items.quote: I think the right way to look at it is, by end of this financial year, I think the 3rd Quarter onwards, things should start looking up much better.

items.statement: Plans rights issue in Q2 FY26 with promoter participation.
items.quote: The Board Committe e has been formed to oversee this capital raise, including a possible righ ts issue in Q2 FY '26. This rights issue will be done with the promoter participation

items.statement: Shareholder approval for capital raise up to Rs. 750 crores.
items.quote: We have received shareholder approval for capital raise during March for up to Rs. 750 crores.

items.statement: Marginal cost of borrowings at 11.9% for Q4 FY25.
items.quote: Our marginal cost of borrowings for the quarter was at 11.9%, which was about 20 bps higher than Q4 of FY ’24 and about 20 bps higher than Q3 FY ‘25.

items.statement: No need to change pricing to borrowers.
items.quote: I don't see a need or a reason right now to look at the pricing at the borrower level.

items.statement: Industry expected to grow 10-15%.
items.quote: I think the industry is slated to grow, let's say, between 10% to 15% with the kind of customer base we have and the numbers that we have kind of put up on the slide, both in terms of existing borrowers and the number of borrowers that we would want to bring on board.

items.statement: Covenant breaches total Rs. 438 crores.
items.quote: The number stacks up presently at Rs. 438 crores in total where Rs. 260 crores is from the capital markets and about Rs. 178 crores from the term lending side.

items.statement: Employee attrition was 56% in previous financial year.
items.quote: Yes, there have been attritions ,. I mean the percentage terms, it was very high for the previous financial year, 56%.

items.statement: Weekly branches have 14% of business.
items.quote: We have about 14% of our business in weekly branches.

items.statement: Liquidity over Rs. 2,000 crores, 24% of assets.
items.quote: Our liquidity position at the end of March 2025 were over Rs. 2,000 crores, which is about 24% of our assets on our balance sheet.

items.statement: Capital adequacy at 37%.
items.quote: We are comfortably placed in terms of capital adequacy at 37% and close to Rs. 2,000 crores in liquidity.

items.statement: Expects PBT margin around 15%.
items.quote: So it is safe to have a guidance of approximately 15%. And there are other shipyards who are listed and you can look at their profit margins and you can gauge what is the general range.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected around 8% to 10% every year.
items.quote: But by and large we will see that the growth of the company is almost around 8% to 10% every year.

items.statement: Order book expected to increase from Rs. 32,000 crore to more than Rs. 1.25 lakh crores if submarine contracts signed.
items.quote: And that is expected to increase our order book from the present Rs. 32,000 crore to more than Rs. 1.25 lakh crores.

items.statement: CAPEX of approximately Rs. 4,000 crores planned.
items.quote: So that is one area and we have also taken up l and from the port for taking up small ships and we are also doing having major CAPEX plans in that land as well as in the N hava yard which we have which we have a CAPEX of approximately Rs. 4,000 crores.

items.statement: Navy likely to issue RFP for 17 Bravo frigates (Rs. 70,000 crore) and MCMV project (Rs. 44,000 crore) shortly.
items.quote: And as you've seen, both the Navy is likely to come out with the RFP for the 17 Bravo frigates shortly, which is a 70,000 crore project. And we are poised best to take on that although it is going to come on a competitive bidding but MDL with its proven capability and infrastructure and having demonstrated to have cons tructed and delivered these ships profitably we are best placed to actually win

items.statement: P-75 additional submarines contract expected to be signed as early as next month, value Rs. 30,000-40,000 crores.
items.quote: Yes, it's expected to be in the range of anywhere between 30,000 crores to 40,000 crores.

items.statement: Margins and profitability expected to significantly improve as major orders materialize.
